10.1109/tkde.2026.3756090: Federated recommendation (FR) is a promising paradigm to protect user privacy in recommender systems. Distinct from general federated scenarios, FR inherently needs to preserve client-specific parameters,i.e., user embeddings, for privacy and personalization. However, we empirically find that globally aggregated item embeddings can induce skew in user embeddings, resulting in suboptimal performance. To this end, we theoretically analyze theuser embedding skewissue and proposePersonalizedFederated recommendation withCalibration viaLow-Rank decomposition (PFedCLR). Specifically, PFedCLR introduces an integrated dual-function mechanism, implemented with a buffer matrix, to jointly calibrate local user embedding and personalize global item embeddings. To ensure efficiency, we employ a low-rank decomposition of the buffer matrix to reduce the model overhead. Furthermore, for privacy, we train and upload the local model before personalization, preventing the server from accessing sensitive information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PFedCLR effectively mitigates user embedding skew and achieves a desirable trade-off among performance, efficiency, and privacy, outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.
10.1109/ton.2026.3756120: Multi-level learning/optimization, e.g., bilevel optimization, has been recognized for its versatile applicability across a broad array of domains, spanning from signal processing to machine learning. However, most existing works focus on bilevel and trilevel optimization. In contrast, multi-level optimization problems involving four or more hierarchical levels, which we term poly-level learning (PLL) problems, remain largely unexplored.In addition, in practical PLL, data may be distributed across multiple nodes over a distributed network. Nevertheless, extant studies on PLL predominantly focus on the non-federated setting, necessitating the collection of data to central servers and thereby posing potential privacy risks. To this end, we propose a Federated Poly-Level Learning (FPLL) framework over a distributed network to tackle the PLL problems with soft constraints in a federated manner. FPLL hinges on a novel non-linear cut, i.e., $L$-cut, for the level-wise relaxation to the PLL problems. Additionally, the proposed federated algorithm is designed with adjustable parameters that allow for a flexible trade-off between its computational complexity and performance efficiency, enabling users to tune it according to specific application requirements. We also carry out non-asymptotic analysis to derive the iteration complexity for the proposed FPLL to achieve the $ε$-Pareto stationary point. Extensive experiments have been undertaken to elucidate the superior efficacy of the proposed method.
10.1109/tcomm.2026.3755517: This paper investigates over-the-air (OTA) computation enabled online federated learning (FL) in low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Specifically, we consider a dual-layer OTA aggregation architecture, where ground devices upload analog model updates to serving satellites via uplink OTA aggregation, and satellites forward the aggregated signals to a data processing center through the second round OTA aggregation. Then, we formulate a long-term data-utilization maximization problem in which devices continuously collect new data and untrained samples gradually lose freshness. The problem is subject to the satellite beam budget, transmit-power limit, and global mean squared error (MSE) constraint that governs end-to-end aggregation distortion. This yields a coupled mixedinteger nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, involving tightly coupled discrete beam-hopping decisions and continuous power control. Due to the combinatorial action space and non-convex constraints, the problem is NP-hard and computationally intractable. Furthermore, the time-varying satellite topology and dynamic data generation render it a sequential decision-making problem, necessitating adaptive online scheduling. To address these issues, we cast the problem as a Markov decision process and develop a proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based deep reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes adaptive beam hopping and power control, using an MSE-aware reward to balance data utilization and aggregation accuracy. Numerical simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms other benchmark schemes, achieving superior long-term data utilization and faster FL convergence while satisfying the MSE requirement.
10.1109/tnsm.2026.3755818: Federated learning provides a privacy-preserving paradigm for Wi-Fi RSSI fingerprint-based indoor localization, but remains vulnerable to stealthy backdoor attacks. In federated RSSI localization, environmental variation, device heterogeneity, and sampling-condition differences cause benign client updates to fluctuate across communication rounds, complicating malicious-update discrimination based on single-round statistics. To address this challenge, we propose FedLoc-Guard, a server-side defense framework that models client reliability from server-observable behavior across rounds. FedLoc-Guard estimates instantaneous reliability from directional consistency, relative update magnitude, and normalized turnaround-time consistency, updates client reliability across rounds, and uses the resulting reliability states for high-reliability client retention and risk-constrained aggregation with pre-normalization weight clipping. The method requires neither previously trusted clients nor an additional clean server-side reference set. Experiments on UJIIndoorLoc and Mall under IID and non-IID settings demonstrate that FedLoc-Guard substantially reduces attack success rates against BadNets, Scaling Attack, DBA, and an A3FL-inspired adaptive backdoor attack while maintaining useful localization performance under the evaluated settings, thereby improving the reliability and trustworthiness of federated indoor localization services.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3755226: Federated learning (FL) is a promising distributed learning paradigm that enables multiple devices to collaboratively train a global model without sharing local private data. Considering the device heterogeneity in computation and communication capabilities, asynchronous aggregation is introduced in FL to improve the learning efficiency. However, asynchronous FL suffers from communication bottlenecks due to limited wireless resources. To address this issue, we propose AQAFL, an adaptive quantization method for asynchronous FL, while also integrating device scheduling and wireless resource allocation. We first present a convergence analysis of asynchronous FL with quantized transmission, and then formulate an optimization problem to minimize the convergence upper bound under long-term latency and bandwidth constraints by jointly optimizing the quantization bit width, device scheduling, and wireless bandwidth allocation. Following that, we analytically characterize the optimal bandwidth allocation and prove that it can be obtained via bisection search, and derive the closed-form expression for the quantization bit width. Subsequently, an efficient device scheduling strategy is proposed to determine the number of participating devices in each round. Experiments show that compared with other methods, AQAFL reduces the total communication overhead by up to 69% and the overhead required to achieve the same target test accuracy by 32.6%–88.6%, while improving test accuracy by 4.1%–6.5%.
10.1109/tsusc.2026.3755693: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) faces severe challenges, including high vehicle mobility, network instability, and massive sensitive data. While centralized federated learning (FL) offers privacy protection, it suffers from limited vehicle computing power and high data redundancy. To solve these issues, we propose DecFLDiff, an edge-assisted decentralized semi-supervised federated learning framework enhanced by a conditional diffusion model. In DecFLDiff, the semi-supervised classifier is trained offline at the edge server and deployed to vehicles in inference-only mode for pseudo-label generation, reducing the need for local vehicle training and making intelligent transportation systems more efficient and reliable in data-driven decision-making. Uploaded feature embeddings are perturbed with Gaussian noise before transmission, which helps preserve local distribution cues while reducing reconstruction risk. By implementing an adaptive hybrid topology, DecFLDiff flexibly adjusts to node density to balance information propagation speed and communication overhead among neighboring nodes and reduce redundant transmissions. By shifting computation-intensive learning and synthetic-data generation to resource-rich edge servers and reducing unnecessary peer-to-peer communication, DecFLDiff improves the overall computational and communication efficiency of decentralized learning in resource-constrained IoV environments. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 show that DecFLDiff outperforms representative decentralized federated-learning baselines under low-label regimes, boosting accuracy by 4%–17% and achieving faster convergence in terms of communication rounds in the reported experimental settings.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3755968: Paging is a fundamental component of Next Generation Mobile Communication Systems (6G, NGMCS), enabling the support of the Internet of Everything (IoE) and ultra-reliable low-latency communications (uRLLC). However, existing paging mechanisms cannot simultaneously satisfy the requirements of paging efficiency, privacy preservation, and service resilience in the distributed architecture of 6G networks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Resilient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Intelligent Paging Mechanism (SecureFedIPM). First, SecureFedIPM builds upon our previous intelligent trajectory-prediction foundation to predict user equipment (UE) trajectories and optimize paging areas, while extending the paging formulation with resilience-aware constraints under node failures and external availability attacks. Based on the hierarchical federated paging architecture, a Hierarchical Privacy-Preserving Paging Architecture (HPPP) is further developed to support distributed collaborative learning while strengthening privacy protection through model-update clipping and differential privacy. Furthermore, a Dynamic Resilience Strategy (DRS) is integrated into HPPP to mitigate performance degradation under node failures and external availability attacks through adaptive aggregation and rapid recovery mechanisms. Experimental results on a real-world telecom dataset demonstrate that, under normal operating conditions ($F=0$), SecureFedIPM reduces paging signaling resources by 74.1% and paging delay by 35.6%. Under node failures and external availability attacks, SecureFedIPM degrades more slowly than the compared intelligent paging schemes, demonstrating its ability to maintain paging services under adverse conditions.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3750699: Decentralized personalized federated learning (DPFL) enables devices to exchange knowledge over peer-to-peer links while retaining client-specific models. Its effectiveness, however, can be impaired by heterogeneous data: indiscriminate neighbor aggregation may introduce negative transfer. This work studies how a client can form a useful collaboration set under this heterogeneity. We proposeAFIND+(Adaptive, Filtered, and Intelligent Neighbor Discovery and Aggregation), a three-stage framework that (i) ranks candidate neighbors using a lightweight proxy of their update representation, (ii) adaptively filters the candidates through a confidence-dependent acceptance threshold, and (iii) aggregates the retained models with loss-based Boltzmann weights. The three stages serve complementary purposes: the first seeks low-discrepancy collaborators, the second controls the participation level, and the third distinguishes contributions within the selected set. Under smoothness and explicit stochastic and collaboration-error conditions, we establish a non-asymptotic bound for average personalized first-order stationarity, separating proxy/coreset, threshold-selection, aggregation, and local-update errors. Experiments on heterogeneous image and text benchmarks show improved accuracy and fewer rounds to a target accuracy relative to the evaluated DPFL baselines.AFIND+is designed as a communication-and-aggregation module that can be combined with personalized learning backbones.
10.1109/tip.2026.3753090: Conventional facial expression recognition (FER) methods often train the model on large-scale centralized expression data. However, expression data are often distributed across heterogeneous devices and incrementally collected in practice. In this paper, we study a little-studied yet important task named federated class-incremental FER (FCI-FER), which aims to incrementally identify unseen compound expressions with the model initially trained on easily accessible basic expressions under the federated learning settings. To address the unique problems of catastrophic forgetting and heterogeneous disturbances across clients in FCI-FER, we propose a disentanglement-guided multi-teacher relational distillation (DMT-RD) method which follows a novel "distillation and disentanglement" paradigm. For local training, we design a multi-teacher hypergraph relational distillation (MTD) module to capture semantic relations between expressions and learn expression features. Meanwhile, we develop a disturbance encoding (DE) module to learn client-specific disturbance information. By minimizing the mutual information (MI) loss between the outputs of the MTD and DE modules, we can achieve feature disentanglement and reduce the negative influence of specific disturbances on local training. For global training, we introduce a multi-teacher learning strategy by clustering historical clients to comprehensively capture client diversity across communication rounds. Our method can effectively preserve old knowledge while learning new compound expressions under federated settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method against several state-of-the-art federated class-incremental learning methods on benchmark datasets.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3755564: Federated training of variational autoencoders (VAEs) must share distributional knowledge across clients without centralizing data or repeatedly exchanging high-dimensional model parameters. Under non-IID data, full-parameter federated optimization is communication-heavy, and clients can learn incompatible latent spaces that slow convergence and degrade reconstruction and generation. We propose SemFedVAE, a communication-efficient, personalized federated VAE framework in which clients keep their own encoders and decoders and share only latent posterior statistics. The server aggregates the semantic means and standard deviations, combining scales in the log-variance domain, into a global latent target. A global consistency (GC) term in the evidence lower bound (ELBO) aligns each local latent distribution with this target by minimizing their KL divergence. We analyze the communication complexity and show that, for bounded GC weights, the regularizer preserves the standard non-convex convergence order. Experiments on six datasets with 5–20 clients show that SemFedVAE reduces the per-round training payload by four to five orders of magnitude relative to full-parameter protocols that train a shareable global model, while remaining competitive in reconstruction and generation quality; a client without local data instead requires a one-time model transfer. Ablations compare the aggregation rule with variance-based alternatives and examine the GC strength and the label-aware extension.
10.1109/tpds.2026.3755398: Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple devices to collaboratively train a shared model for downstream tasks while preserving data privacy. However, the substantial memory footprint during the local training process hinders resource-limited devices from participating, thereby significantly degrading model performance. This paper introducesBlockFormer, an innovative FL framework designed to overcome memory constraints, enhancing both model performance and training efficiency. Rather than training the shared model from scratch, BlockFormer constructs the global model by assembling pre-trained neural network blocks, tailored to the data distributed across participating clients in order to deliver better memory and computing efficiency. Specifically, BlockFormer features three core components: 1) Client Grouper, 2) Adapter Configurator, and 3) Inference Accelerator. On the server side, the Client Grouper is designed to handle data heterogeneity in FL by clustering clients based on data distribution and strategically selecting participants in each round to enhance data diversity during training. On the client side, the Adapter Configurator ensures network blocks with different structures can be concatenated without sacrificing performance by designing tailored adapters based on their structural and dimensional differences. Moreover, the Inference Accelerator is deployed to reduce the additional computational overhead and latency introduced by block assembling, enhancing overall inference efficiency. It consists of two modules: the Model Fusioner optimizes multi-model inference introduced by block selection at the computation graph level through merging highly correlated computation nodes; the Resource Scheduler optimizes GPU execution by dynamically adjusting scheduling strategies based on task dependencies, ensuring efficient resource utilization and minimizing execution bottlenecks. Extensive experiments on representative datasets and edge devices demonstrate that compared to existing approaches, BlockFormer improves the model accuracy by up to 33.88%, achieves up to 17.94× speedup, and significantly reduces the memory footprint by up to 91% during the learning procedure.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3754357: Federated learning over heterogeneous edge net works is often limited by persistent communication imbalance. Devices with weak terrestrial connectivity may repeatedly miss upload deadlines and become underrepresented in global training. Existing terrestrial scheduling methods can improve resource utilization, but they still operate within the available ground network and cannot always recover devices whose terrestrial links remain infeasible. Satellite assisted federated learning provides wider communication coverage, but existing studies mainly focus on satellite resource coordination, hierarchical aggregation, or data offloading. They provide limited support for selectively using satellite access to recover long term participation of communication constrained ground devices. To address this problem, we propose FASAFL, a fairness aware Starlink assisted federated learning framework. FASAFL explicitly models Starlink as a dynamic and resource constrained uplink by incorporating satellite visibility, shared beam capacity, handover, gateway routing, weather conditions, and retransmission reliability into the access decision. The server selectively assigns Starlink to devices whose terrestrial links restrict timely participation, rather than treating satellite access as a uniformly better communication option. FASAFL further integrates learning value, resource expenditure, and participation history into the scheduling process, so that current satellite allocation is jointly coordinated with the long term participation of communication constrained devices. The server also uses bounded quality aware compensation during scheduling and aggregation to increase the opportunities of persistently underrepresented devices without giving excessive influence to stale or low quality updates. Experiments on four datasets with Hypatia and ns-3 based dynamic LEO simulations show that FASAFL improves effective participation, learning performance, fairness, and deadline reliability under limited satellite resources.
10.1109/tcyb.2026.3750279: Federated learning (FL) is a prominent machine learning (ML) framework that enables training a global model across distributed client devices without exposing their private data. However, traditional FL methods often face challenges in achieving fast convergence, particularly in heterogeneous or non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data environments. These issues arise primarily from inaccurate gradient estimation during the optimization process. To address these limitations, this article introduces an adaptive optimizer, federated fractional gradient descent with adaptive parameter updates (FedFGD-APUs). In particular, the proposed FedFGD-APU optimizer leverages fractional-order derivatives for efficient gradient computation. It employs an adaptive strategy to dynamically adjust fractional order, learning rate, and momentum to improve learning convergence and stability. We also develop a theoretical computational framework linking federated optimization with adaptive fractional derivatives, establishing the convergence of FedFGD-APU for nonconvex optimization settings with a convergence rate of $\mathcal {O}(1/T)$ . We conduct comprehensive experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and NSL-KDD datasets to validate FedFGD-APU's effectiveness under both IID and non-IID data distributions. The experimental results demonstrate that FedFGD-APU significantly improves communication speedups and testing accuracy across heterogeneous data scenarios.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3754440: In edge computing, data Replication Coding (RC) represents the overarching redundancy management paradigm for guaranteeing data availability and reliability, while Erasure Coding (EC) constitutes a more storage-efficient redundancy mechanism for implementing this paradigm. To bridge the gap where conventional EC and RC schemes prioritize fault tolerance at the expense of data privacy and model integrity, we propose a Federated Learning-driven failure prediction mechanism. By enabling edge nodes to perform localized training on sensitive data coupled with secure aggregation, our framework constructs a robust global model. This approach achieves collaborative forecasting of regional failures and workload dynamics while strictly maintaining data residency and mitigating the risks of model poisoning and adversarial propagation. Leveraging these predictive insights, we propose HRS, a Security-Aware Hybrid Replication mechanism that dynamically switches between EC and RC modes. HRS incorporates a quantitative security model centered on Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA), employing a cross-domain replica dispersion strategy to mitigate systemic risks from coordinated attacks and large-scale outages. To prevent security-related overheads from compromising system longevity, we further introduce the EMRA module, which utilizes Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) for residual energy forecasting and formulates a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to achieve a Pareto-optimal allocation across energy, latency, and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that HRS-EMRA maintains data residency and enhances resilience against poisoning and DDoS attacks, while achieving more than 90% data availability and a 13.2% 23.9% reduction in energy consumption. With end-to-end latency capped at 74.32 ms, our framework validates its efficacy in harmonizing privacy preservation, secure replication, and efficient resource orchestration.
10.1109/tcc.2026.3754858: Federated learning (FL) aggregation on serverless platforms faces a hard scalability ceiling: existing architectures ($\lambda$-FL, LIFL) partitionclientsacross aggregators, but every aggregator must hold the complete model gradient in memory. When gradients exceed the per-function memory limit (e.g., 10 GB on AWS Lambda), aggregation becomes infeasible regardless of tree depth or branching factor. We propose GRADSSHARDING, which instead partitions thegradient tensorinto$M$shards, each averaged independently by a serverless function that receives contributions from all clients. Because FedAvg averaging is element-wise, this produces bit-identical results to tree-based approaches, so model accuracy is invariant by construction. Per-function memory is bounded at$\mathcal {O}(|\theta |/M)$, independent of client count, removing the per-function memory ceiling that limits full-gradient architectures. We evaluate GRADSSHARDING against$\lambda$-FL and LIFL through HPC experiments and real AWS Lambda deployments across model sizes from 43 MB to 5 GB. Results show a cost crossover at$\sim$500 MB gradient size, 2.7× cost reduction at VGG-16 scale, and that GRADSSHARDING is the only architecture that remains deployable beyond the serverless memory ceiling.
10.1109/tr.2026.3753241: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralising user data, but incross-devicesettings the large and volatile client population makes training slow and unreliable. Two factors dominate: (i) many devices are offline when polled, and (ii) the online devices differ widely in compute and network speed. We introduceTiFL–MDA, a composite client-selection strategy thatjointlytackles these hurdles. First,Tier-based FL (TiFL)groups clients into latency tiers that reflect their resource profiles; then theMust-Detect-Availability (MDA)filter chooses the most responsive clientswithin each tier. By coupling resource awareness and availability detection, TiFL–MDA maximises parallelism without sacrificing fairness. Across five datasets and six heterogeneity settings, TiFL–MDA reaches target accuracy in up to6.5 % fewer communication roundsthan vanilla FL and improves final accuracy by up to23 %. Unlike 'fast-only' selection, our tier-aware design prevents bias towards high-end devices.
10.1109/tce.2026.3754565: Automobile insurance claim prediction require sufficient quality data from various data curators (e.g., insurance companies and telematics providers) to build effective models. However, the intermittent communication bandwidth, privacy and security issues are the main obstacles to the information sharing. The reliability and efficiency of data sharing need to be further enhanced. In this paper, we propose FedAuto, a sequential horizontal-vertical Federated Learning (FL) framework to relieve transmission load and address privacy concerns of data holding parties for claim prediction in automobile insurance industry. Differing from existing FL methods that only support single data partition mode, FedAuto constructs a tightly coupled end-to-end workflow for domain business requirements, can jointly handle horizontal and vertical data separations. In particular, we develop an adaptive differential privacy enhanced horizontal FL for multi-drivers’ collaborative behavior risk prediction and a clustering-optimized encrypted vertical FL for accurate claim prediction, together with an architectural interface for passing HFL-derived driving-risk features to VFL claim-cost modeling. Finally, extensive experiments on public datasets show that FedAuto achieves a 9.35× reduction in HFL readiness-collection time relative to synchronous baselines and a 18.11× reduction in the calculated VFL full-tree payload upper bound relative to SecureBoost.
10.1109/tii.2026.3747685: Smart-grid services increasingly rely on distributed learning, but pooling regional load records, operating parameters, and topology information can violate privacy and critical-infrastructure constraints. Federated learning avoids direct data sharing, yet local updates remain exposed to gradient inversion, protected aggregation limits the observability of Byzantine poisoning and free-riding behavior, and static blockchain trust can be strategically manipulated. This article proposes privacy-enhanced federated learning with dynamic reputation consensus for secure smart-grid collaboration. Its protected update path combines integral affine-bijective grouped encoding, participant-specific masking, Paillier aggregation, and Shamir-based mask recovery to reduce encrypted payloads, retain a masking layer after private-key exposure when masks remain unavailable, and tolerate participant dropout. A benchmark-model-driven Euclidean distance and cosine similarity audit converts complementary magnitude and directional evidence into cross-round reputation for validator and leader selection and deposit-based incentives. Experiments on heterogeneous image benchmarks and two real-world load-forecasting tasks show stable utility under non-IID data, independent, mixed, and delayed strategic poisoning, and dropout rates up to 30%. In the evaluated LeNet-5 configuration, the encrypted payload decreases from 812.19 MiB for parameterwise Paillier-FedAvg to 7.96 MiB per client per round. Under the evaluated attack conditions, the key-exposure test yields distorted reconstructions. The election tests show close agreement between empirical and theoretical leader-election probabilities.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3753963: Federated learning (FL) enables edge devices (EDs) in mobile edge computing (MEC) networks to collaboratively train a shared model without exchanging raw data. However, heterogeneous computing and communication capabilities, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and limited wireless resources introduce straggler delays, stale updates, and client drift, thereby increasing convergence latency. To address these challenges, we propose SAFL-HACM, a semi-asynchronous FL framework with a heterogeneity-aware coordination mechanism for MEC networks. SAFL-HACM allows EDs to train independently and buffers their completed updates for selective aggregation without interrupting ongoing local training. It coordinates three components: 1) a local drift control mechanism that combines update-direction correction with a stateful drift variable to mitigate non-IID-induced drift and stale-model inconsistency; 2) a cluster-balanced scheduling strategy that jointly considers data-distribution representation, update staleness, local training utility, and participation history; and 3) a latency-aware bandwidth allocation scheme that minimizes the completion time of each aggregation cycle under a limited uplink bandwidth budget. Experiments across four benchmark datasets and different levels of data heterogeneity show that SAFL-HACM reduces convergence latency by 64.0% on average over representative baselines. Moreover, across different device scales, it improves test accuracy by an average of 6.5% while maintaining robust performance.
10.1109/tits.2026.3745265: In the field of intelligent vehicles, collecting data to optimize the user experience often raises regulation and privacy issues, hindering effective data utilization. This paper presents a blockchain-based regulatory computing framework for privacy-preserving data sharing among intelligent vehicles. First, a federated learning environment is established on the basis of blockchain. This environment effectively addresses regulation issues and provides an infrastructure for the responsible use of intelligent vehicle data. A secure aggregation method is then introduced on the basis of grouped Shamir secret sharing. This method addresses the critical issue of privacy data leakage, ensuring that user data are well protected during sharing. Moreover, we explore incentive mechanisms and weight distribution strategies. The incentive mechanism aims to encourage active collaboration among participants, and the weight distribution strategy ensures optimal results during the training process and supports sustainable development. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system, we conduct a series of experiments using different datasets. The results show that our mechanism performs exceptionally well in terms of key performance indicators such as performance, latency, and training effectiveness while also providing sufficient data protection. This study offers a reliable method of regulation and privacy protection for intelligent vehicle data.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3754070: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are widely utilized in various Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, such as face recognition, speech assistant, and autonomous driving. However, recent studies reveal DNN's vulnerability to backdoor attacks, also known as trojan attacks. A backdoored DNN makes wrong predictions when the input contains the trigger, which poses significant security threats to DNN-based AI systems. Existing backdoor removal methods often require access to clean validation samples or samples with the trigger. However, this may not be feasible in some real-world scenarios, such as when dealing with models from online platforms or federated learning environments. To bridge this critical gap, we propose DeepSanitizer, which introduces a new algorithmic formulation for data-free backdoor mitigation. Unlike prior detection-focused workFreeEagle, DeepSanitizer shifts the paradigm directly to backdoor removal. Rather than merely applying known reverseengineering techniques to reconstruct triggers or integrating existing pruning models into a pipeline, DeepSanitizer synthesizes benign dummy representations to fine-tune the compromised model classifier. This enables the mitigation of diverse backdoor attacks without the need for access to either clean or poisoned data. Specifically, our method splits a compromised model into two components: the feature extractor and the model classifier via an introduced inspection layer. Then it utilizes a novel gradient-based algorithm to generate feature representations as the dummy data for fine-tuning the model classifier to remove the backdoor. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach effectively removes planted backdoors while maintaining the model performance, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art data-free and non-data-free backdoor mitigation techniques. Finally, DeepSanitizer reduces the defense time to just minutes, greatly faster than the existing methods.
10.1109/twc.2026.3754365: Over-the-air (OTA) computation has recently gained significant attentions as an effective approach to enhance the communication efficiency of wireless federated learning (FL). By enabling simultaneous transmission and aggregation of local model updates, OTA-FL can substantially reduce both latency and bandwidth consumption. However, a key challenge lies in the imperfect aggregation of global models caused by channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, which introduces distortion to the final learning performance. To address this issue, we study the long-term mean squared error (MSE) minimization problem for OTA-FL under imperfect CSI conditions. Through convergence analysis, we establish an upper bound for the time-averaged MSE, thereby revealing the effect of aggregation errors accumulated throughout multiple communication rounds on the overall training performances. Based on this analysis, an optimization framework is developed to minimize the long-term MSE via the joint design of (i) transmit coefficients at the local devices and (ii) receive combining vectors at the parameter server (PS). Since this alternating optimization approach requires non-causal CSI, a Lyapunov-based optimization method is further introduced to handle causal CSI scenarios. By incorporating virtual queues to characterize long-term energy consumption, the proposed method effectively decouples temporal dependencies and allows transmit coefficients to be optimized based on the causal CSI of each aggregation round. Comprehensive evaluations on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets have demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the degradation of test accuracy caused by imperfect CSI. Comparisons with other benchmark schemes further verify the superiority of our proposed algorithms.
10.1109/tcc.2026.3753585: Detecting zero-day attacks in federated streaming networks is challenging because clients observe heterogeneous and evolving traffic, while ground-truth labels for incoming traffic may be delayed, limited, or unavailable for subsequent model updating and evaluation. We propose FedTrident, a communication-efficient open-world federated intrusion detection system that combines personalized per-class reconstruction with federated threshold calibration. Each client maintains private class-specific autoencoders and learns class-aware rejection thresholds from known-class traffic. Federation exchanges only one scalar threshold per known class, rather than raw data, gradients, embeddings, prototypes, or model parameters. During streaming inference, FedTrident identifies the best-matching class using reconstruction error and makes an online known/unknown decision based on the corresponding threshold. Rejected samples can subsequently undergo guarded novelty discovery without altering the immediate decision. We evaluate FedTrident across CICIDS2018, 5G-NIDD, ToN-IoT, and Edge-IIoTset under stationary non-IID, concept-drift, and zero-day evolution scenarios. The results show that per-class reconstruction and federated thresholding provide a useful balance between known-class recognition, false-unknown control, and open-world detection while substantially reducing communication relative to full model exchange.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3753654: The verifiable and lightweight multi-round secure federated learning framework proposed by Li et al. is claimed to achieve dropout resilience, lightweight parameter reuse, and verification of the server's aggregation results. However, this comment identifies plaintext-gradient leakage caused by the combination of long-term private key reconstruction during dropout recovery and cross-round key reuse. Consequently, the aggregation server (AS) can use the reconstructed long-term private key to recover the client's plaintext gradient when the client participates in a later round. Theoretical analysis shows that this plaintext-gradient leakage occurs under both the malicious and the honest-but-curious (HBC) AS threat models.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3753855: As the low-altitude economy expands, Low-Altitude Wireless Networks (LAWN) are critical for UAV-based emergency response, particularly for pixel-level semantic segmentation in complex post-disaster environments. However, multi-UAV collaborative perception faces a fundamental computation-communication trade-off. Heavy local computing induces significant processing latency on resource-constrained UAVs, while offloading raw data to a central server suffers from the limited and stochastic capacity of individual air-to-ground channels. Additionally, heterogeneous data transmission delays inevitably lead to spatiotemporal asynchronous deviations among collaborative nodes. To resolve these conflicts, we propose a Federated Variational Inference (FVI) framework that effectively balances model complexity and communication overhead. Instead of exchanging high-dimensional features and model parameters, UAVs distill statistical intent probability vectors for semantic communication. By reasoning in the federated posterior domain, these vectors support uncertainty-aware semantic fusion at the ground server, enabling lightweight collaborative perception. Extensive experiments on a UAV swarm testbed show that, under the evaluated non-IID and channel settings, FVI-Net achieves up to an 18.97 percentage-point improvement in mIoU over the strongest baseline. Results validate the effectiveness of posterior-domain semantic fusion for communication-efficient and robust UAV swarm perception in constrained LAWN scenarios.
10.1109/tkde.2026.3753678: In distributed data stream processing, buffered asynchronous aggregation collects the first returned updates into a buffer and treats them as a representative sample of the population. Under non-IID data and system heterogeneity, this latency-selected stream can be temporally fresh yet statistically unrepresentative: fast client groups may dominate the buffer while slower groups carrying complementary population directions are systematically absent. We formalize this failure mode asdirection-level representation skewand propose DirBridge, a server-side stream-summary framework that corrects the bias without delaying aggregation or storing per-client entire caches. DirBridge compresses update directions with Count Sketch features, clusters clients into spherical direction groups, and refills only the missing group mass using exponential-moving-average (EMA) group memories. The abstraction is group-based rather than identity-based, reducing auxiliary server storage. We show that group-size-aware refill can eliminate the mixture-weight error under an ideal representative condition, and we further bound the residual convergence error. Experiments on vision, character recognition, and speech workloads under synthetic and natural latency traces show that DirBridge improves stream representativeness when direction skew is large, preserves accuracy when skew is low, and incurs modest overhead. These results position direction-group memory as a practical bias-correction abstraction for latency-selected distributed data streams.
10.1109/tfuzz.2026.3752321: Federated learning ensures data privacy but its effectiveness may be compromised under non-IID heterogeneity, which motivates adaptive server-side aggregation. However OWA, despite its rank-based coordinate-wise flexibility, is difficult to deploy because selecting effective weights is non-trivial and fixed profiles may not match round-to-round changes in client update distributions. This paper proposes an online and lightweight adaptation strategy for OWA weights, parameterized by a single temperature variable that generates a smooth, monotonically decreasing weight vector. At each communication round, the server evaluates a small set of candidate temperatures using a held-out proxy set and selects the one that minimizes proxy loss, with exponential smoothing to stabilize the temperature over time. Experiments conducted on 10 classification benchmark datasets under non-IID partitions show that the proposed adaptive variant achieves statistically significant improvements over all considered reference methods at the global level. Aggregated across datasets, FedOWA Adapt improves mean accuracy by approximately 3.3 percentage points over FedAvg and 1.9 percentage points over fixed-weight FedOWA. In terms of log-loss, the proposed method reduces the mean loss by about 0.12 compared with FedAvg and by about 0.15 compared with fixed-weight FedOWA, indicating improved predictive reliability in addition to higher accuracy. The largest dataset-level gains are particularly visible on selected benchmarks, reaching approximately 13.5 percentage points over FedAvg and up to about 7.8 percentage points over fixed-weight FedOWA. Furthermore, a detailed one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analysis and an ablation study were performed, confirming the robustness of the proposed configuration and showing that the main source of improvement is the repeated round-wise adaptation of the OWA aggregation profile rather than a single fixed or one-shot selected weighting scheme.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3752488: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) are vulnerable to Global Positioning System (GPS) spoofing attacks that threaten navigation integrity. Existing detection approaches face challenges in privacy, computational efficiency, and class imbalance. We propose three progressive frameworks: 1) a lightweight standalone Logistic Regression (LR) model achieving 95.52% accuracy; 2) Federated Learning with LR (FL+LR), which enables collaborative training across CAVs while keeping raw data local and achieves 97.25% accuracy; 3) a Digital Twin-enhanced framework (DT+FL+LR), which integrates simulated spoofing scenarios and DT-based consistency checking and achieves 97.46% accuracy. Evaluation on AVG-Dataset-1 (62,042 samples) shows that DT+FL+LR achieves 90.00% spoofed-class recall and 100.00% precision. The computational analysis indicates potential edge deployment suitability for standalone LR under the evaluated configuration, while FL variants provide improved data locality with competitive performance. Across the evaluated configurations, the AUC increases from 95.02% to 98.10%, indicating improved discrimination capability and potential deployment feasibility under the considered experimental configuration.
10.1109/tcc.2026.3753332: Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) and Vehicular-Fogs (VFs) are placed nearer to user equipment (UE), reducing propagation latency compared to traditional cloud-based systems and ensuring a high standard of Quality of Service (QoS). Nevertheless, MEC sites can become congested and overloaded during peak traffic periods, such as concerts or sporting events. To address this, offloading techniques can shift intensive computational tasks from devices with limited resources to those with greater capacity, enhancing task performance and thereby increasing battery longevity. This study investigates the offloading within a two-tier framework of MEC and VF, focusing on the offloading of MEC to VF. Maintaining QoS is challenging due to the instability of fog networks caused by high-speed vehicle movement, which disrupts both vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communications. To mitigate this, we analyze vehicle mobility using a Gauss-Markov Mobility (GMM) model. Our main goal is to reduce the normalized system cost by optimizing both latency and energy consumption while accounting for vehicle mobility. We approach this challenge as a multi-objective optimization problem and develop a reinforcement learning environment. Additionally, we propose an algorithm based on imitation learning called Hybrid PSO-TD3, an enhancement of the TD3 algorithm, to effectively manage these complexities.
10.1109/tcc.2026.3752611: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, yet model updates may still leak sensitive information. Multi-key homomorphic encryption (MKHE) can protect updates of clients, but existing works still suffer from complex key management, costly dropout handling, and reliance on an honest-but-curious cloud server. Verifiable MPC-based schemes verify the aggregated client set but incur high communication overhead. TEE-assisted designs enhance efficiency but are bottlenecked by the limited TEE memory and vulnerable to attacks by a malicious cloud server. To address these challenges, we propose TMB-BFV, a TEE-assisted BFV variant incorporating client-specific binding keys, upon which we build AegisFed, a secure FL framework. Specifically, i) to reduce TEE memory usage and computation overhead, we design a lightweight key management mechanism; ii) to resist server–client collusion while making ciphertexts containing different client-specific binding terms homomorphically additive, we optimize the ciphertext structure and introduce an authenticated binding mechanism (ABM); iii) to support arbitrary client dropout without additional handling, we develop a TEE-assisted decryption-share generation mechanism. Finally, we provide formal security analysis and extensive experiments. Compared with the latest TEE-based MKHE scheme, AegisFed resists malicious-server privacy attacks with only minimal additional communication overhead. It also significantly reduces per-client TEE memory consumption and lowers client-side and server-side computation overhead by 20–30% and over 30%, respectively.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3752625: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) trains models collaboratively without a central server, but asymmetric and time-varying communication often leads to imbalanced information flow and biased aggregation. Most existing methods address this issue with push-sum normalization, which requires maintaining auxiliary normalization states and can accumulate numerical drift, thereby slowing mixing and degrading convergence under limited connectivity. To address this, we propose Pull-in protocol, a receiver-driven decentralized learning frame work for directed time-varying graphs. Instead of relying on indiscriminate broadcasting, each receiver actively pulls models from a budgeted subset of incoming neighbors and constructs a row-stochastic aggregation vector locally. This receiver-side normalization makes the model aggregation step a stable convex combination by design and avoids push-sum-type normaliza tion variables in directed model mixing. To mitigate the bias caused by directed and asymmetric aggregation, we incorporate a gradient-tracking correction mechanism. In Pull-in-GT, the model aggregation matrix is row-stochastic, while the tracking matrix is constructed to be column-stochastic, enabling average preservation of the tracking variable over directed graphs. We establish convergence guarantees under standard smooth non convex objectives and bounded stochastic noise. The resulting bound explicitly separates optimization progress from consensus induced error terms and yields the rate O(T−1/2) quantifies the mixing speed of the induced row-stochastic matrix. Extensive experiments on vision-centric decentralized learning benchmarks demonstrate that Pull-in consistently improves training stability and achieves stronger performance than representative push-sum based DFL baselines across a wide range of network asymmetries.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3753237: In Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks (STIN), distributed Federated Edge Learning (FEL) has become mainstream methods for data processing and analysis. The traditional FEL algorithm assigns devices for local training and satellites for aggregation to perform intelligent prediction and decision-making. However, it adopts a synchronous aggregation mechanism, where model updating is performed only after all devices complete training. Considering the heterogeneous computational frequency of devices and the advanced onboard processing capabilities of satellites, satellites act as participants in collaborative local training. In this paper, we introduce a Data Offloading-enabled Federated Edge Learning (DO-FEL) framework, where devices offload part of their data to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. The LEO satellites also act as Edge Servers (ESs), while the Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellite performs global aggregation. In DO-FEL, the dynamic satellite-device visibility and the limited computational frequency of a single satellite incur additional delay for FEL in STIN. Based on this, we propose a Dynamic Route Scheduling (DRS) strategy to optimize multisatellites' assistance for the collaborative training. Meanwhile, we propose an Adaptive Joint Delay-Energy Optimization (AJDEO) strategy. For different task requirements, the AJDEO strategy adjusts the devices' offloading proportion to balance overall delay and energy consumption. Experimental results show that with the DRS strategy, the DO-FEL framework reduces satelliteside delay and further reduces the overall delay. Besides, the proposed framework with two strategies achieves the trade-off between the overall delay and energy consumption compared with other baselines. This paper provides a new perspective for efficient FEL in STIN through flexible data offloading under actual satellite-device visibility.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3753050: Search and rescue (SAR) operations faces many critical challenges due to high-bandwidth sensing, dynamic ocean environments, and strict energy and communication constraints that are encountered in maritime environments. Efficient coordination of Internet-of-Maritime Things (IoMT) devices, especially for guaranteeing the safety of maritime users, is therefore of extreme importance. Traditional approaches treat semantic communication, digital twins, and decentralized control separately, missing opportunities for integrated optimization. In this paper, we propose a semantic-aware digital twin (SemaDT-RL), a unified framework that incorporates variational semantic federated learning, a predictive digital twin, and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning with graph attention networks (MADRL-GAT) for resilient IoMT-driven SAR. The semantic layer compresses sensor data into lightweight anomaly-aware descriptors, drastically reducing bandwidth without sacrificing survivor detection. The predictive digital twin layer assimilates semantic updates using an extended Kalman filter to estimate survivor and node states and generate predictive guidance for survivor tracking and node energy-aware coordination. The MADRL-GAT control layer leverages these forecasts to optimize each node's trajectory, processing, and transmission decisions under mobility, energy, and communication constraints. Extensive simulations demonstrate that SemaDT-RL achieves faster survivor detection, lower communication overhead, and superior energy efficiency compared to baseline methods, demonstrating its effectiveness under the evaluated maritime SAR configuration.
10.1109/tafe.2026.3741470: This article discusses the potential of machine learning (ML) to provide transformative benefits to agricultural development in traditionally data-scarce contexts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Data scarcity is characterized by low-quality, insufficient, or expensive information. In this study, we review a set of ML approaches that are particularly suited to low-resource environments to address these challenges, including transfer learning, few-shot learning, federated learning, synthetic data generation, and active learning (AL). The term “data-scarce intelligence” is defined as the strategic use of ML approaches for obtaining useful insights and enabling intelligent decision-making in environments with little, low-quality, or expensive data. Key Agriculture 4.0 use cases, such as crop yield prediction and plant disease detection, illustrate the significance of these approaches. While ML systems in data-rich contexts often report accuracy levels above 90%, the results discussed here suggest that more modest but still practical performance—typically between 70% and 85%—can be achieved in early-stage, data-limited deployments. However, major obstacles persist, including very low data levels, underdeveloped digital infrastructure, and a lack of local human technological capacity. The article concludes with a roadmap suggestion for effective implementation of ML, which can lead to sustainable changes in agricultural practice and food security in the region.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3752804: In this paper, we propose PVFUnlearn, a privacypreserving and verifiable data circulation framework for edge assisted federated unlearning in hierarchical federated learning systems. Particularly, local model updates are decomposed into sign and magnitude vectors, where additive homomorphic encryption is applied to the magnitude vectors to achieve efficient secure aggregation with reduced cryptographic overhead. To support efficient federated unlearning, edge-level and serverlevel calibration mechanisms are designed in the way that reconstructs calibrated model updates without requiring the participation of clients under non-unlearning edge servers, thereby avoiding expensive retraining from scratch. In addition, homomorphic commitments are integrated into both aggregation and unlearning processes to guarantee aggregation correctness and unlearning verifiability. Extensive experiments conducted on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that PVFUnlearn achieves forgetting performance close to retraining-based federated unlearning while significantly reducing computational and communication overhead. The results further show that PVFUnlearn effectively maintains model utility and provides strong auditability for secure and trustworthy data circulation in edge-assisted federated unlearning systems.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3752851: Federated learning can achieve collaborative training while protecting user privacy and data security, but differences in the performance of participating devices and the diversity of data distributions pose core challenges: 1) highly heterogeneous data reduce the generalization ability of the model; 2) “straggler” clients with limited capabilities or slow responses can significantly affect the system's training stability. However, existing research still cannot collaboratively address these dual issues within a unified framework, resulting in a trade-off between model generalization and system robustness. To tackle these issues, we propose SplitKD, which enhances the model's generalization to data heterogeneity and stability for straggler clients through parameter splitting and freezing, adaptive knowledge distillation, and differentially weighted aggregation. Specifically, SplitKD finely regulates the knowledge transfer from the global model to the local model through parameter splitting and an adaptive knowledge distillation mechanism, enhancing the generalization ability of the model. For straggler clients, we have designed a parameter-splitting-based differentially weighted aggregation strategy that distinguishes model differences by parameters and simultaneously aggregates their local knowledge, enhancing the robustness and compatibility of the global model. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the convergence of SplitKD, and experimental results show that, compared with 12 existing methods, SplitKD effectively mitigates the impact of stragglers on model performance and enhances model generalization.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3752413: Driven by the advancement of Agentic AI, the deployment of autonomous edge agents in safety-critical systems has introduced stringent requirements for privacy-preserving and adaptive intelligence over dynamic and heterogeneous data streams. While Federated Learning (FL) addresses the privacy constraint through collaborative training without sharing raw data, it struggles with the continuously evolving edge data perceived by autonomous agents. To bridge this gap, Federated Continual Learning (FCL) extends the FL paradigm to enable Agentic AI models to incrementally adapt to new tasks and non-stationary distributions, without compromising data privacy. Despite its potential, FCL faces significant challenges in balancing local personalization and global knowledge consolidation, particularly under heterogeneous and imbalanced class distributions across edge agents. Overcoming this dual challenge is critical to robust, adaptive and trustworthy Agentic AI applications at the network edge. In this work, we propose Meta Representation-based Adaptive Personalized Federated Class Incremental Learning (Meta-APFCIL) to tackle these limitations. Each edge agent first performs adaptive meta-training of a shared representation network using its respective exemplar memory within the FL framework. The resulting global representation is then personalized through fine-tuning on each FCL client's current task data and exemplar memory, guided by class-wise logit adjustment to effectively mitigate the bias introduced by class imbalance between current tasks and stored exemplars. As a result, this approach alleviates catastrophic forgetting, enhancing the model's adaptability and retention of previously learned knowledge. Experimental results demonstrate that Meta-APFCIL outperforms key baseline algorithms, achieving an average task accuracy improvement of 23.79% to 32.62% under varying levels of task similarity among clients' data streams. Additionally, it exhibits the lowest task forgetting ratio and the highest generalization capability among FCL clients, enabling trustworthy and adaptive Agentic AI deployment in edge networks.
10.1109/tcomm.2026.3752697: Federated learning (FL) can preserve privacy, but it is limited by the coverage of static edge servers and vulnerable to security risks due to the frequent exchange of model parameters. To address these issues, we establish an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted covert FL framework to protect the transmission of local models from detection by an aerial warden. Acting as a flying server, the UAV aggregates local models from distributed ground devices to improve transmission efficiency. We aim to minimize the energy consumption of terrestrial devices in the presence of a severe security threat to the FL, where the warden adopts the minimum error detection probability. To meet the requirements of energy-sensitive applications, the UAV trajectory, transmission power, local accuracy, model upload time, and local computation capacity are jointly optimized. We decompose the optimization problem into three subproblems, and a low-complexity algorithm is developed. Specifically, for a given UAV trajectory, we derive the closed-form solutions for other variables to reduce the computational complexity. The UAV trajectory is then optimized using successive convex approximation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UAV-assisted covert FL scheme in minimizing the energy consumption while guaranteeing the secrecy.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3752445: Federated learning (FL) allows distributed devices to collaboratively train models while preserving data privacy, but heterogeneous computation and communication resources create stragglers, slowing training and limiting scalability. Existing methods, such as client selection, asynchronous FL, and partial training, partially address this but often reduce accuracy or disrupt model consistency. We propose FedEL++, a federated elastic learning framework that addresses both computation and communication heterogeneity. FedEL++ introduces a globally coordinated sliding window, anchored to the slowest client, and optimizes block window selection across all clients under a unified runtime constraint. Within each window, elastic tensor selection accounts for computation and communication costs, while a global-aware tensor importance adjustment mitigates model drift under non-iid data. Experiments on real edge devices and large-scale simulations show that FedEL++ achieves faster convergence, lower training time, and reduced memory and energy usage, while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared to existing FL methods.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3752495: Federated Learning in Internet-of-Things networks confronts a fundamental spatio-temporal trade-off driven by statistical heterogeneity and severe client participation sparsity. Traditional optimization frameworks struggle between two suboptimal extremes: instantaneous aggregation in Drop mode, which suffers from persistent sampling variance due to tiny active client subsets, and historical caching in Stale mode, which incurs cumulative spatial divergence and staleness bias from outdated local updates. In this paper, we proposeFederated Trajectory-Aware Displacement Aggregation (FedTADA), an optimization framework formulated in cumulative displacement space. To stabilize scale normalization without stochastic feedback loops,FedTADAintroduces a zero-order probing phase that establishes an exogenous energy reference anchor. Guided by an unnormalized negative entropy regularizer, we derive a scale-equivariant exponential controller that dynamically balances instantaneous descent against historical consensus. Theoretical analysis proves thatFedTADAachieves higher-order variance suppression, accelerating the client-sampling variance decay rate from the standard$\mathcal {O}(1/T)$down to$\mathcal {O}(1/T^{2})$via a joint Lyapunov potential function that strictly neutralizes staleness bias while isolating the irreducible Local-SGD drift floor. Extensive experiments across four distinct modalities under fully trainable end-to-end convolutional architectures demonstrate thatFedTADAachieves significant accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under extreme label skew with zero additional client-side computational or communication overhead.
10.1109/tai.2026.3752417: The client selection of federated learning presents a pivotal dilemma necessitating the harmonization of performance and efficiency. Prevailing studies frame this dilemma within the context of a multi-armed bandit optimization problem. With an expanding client base, the complexity of the task increases exponentially, demanding advanced algorithms to efficiently navigate the decision space. Fuzzy sets offer a clear depiction of the uncertainties associated with client selection, eliminating the need for intricate numerical computations. To this end, this paper proposes a fuzzy client selection (FuzzyCS) method. Specifically, we construct a fuzzy multi-criteria information matrix based on several selection criteria and use it to introduce a criteria-oriented fuzzy selection model. By leveraging the fuzzy rough approximations, we can estimate the fuzzy relationship between the criteria-oriented fuzzy concepts of each client and its likelihood of being selected. FuzzyCS can actively balance performance and efficiency by constructing an adaptive fuzzy approximation set, which incorporates the upper and lower approximate fuzzy rough sets. Experimental results demonstrate that FuzzyCS achieves the top Friedman rank in both performance and efficiency. The code is available athttps://github.com/dqlme/FuzzyCS.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3752635: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks; however, training them from scratch requires substantial computational resources. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as an efficient fine-tuning technique that enables the adaptation of pre-trained LLMs to specific tasks with significantly reduced computational cost. In Federated Learning (FL), mobile clients operate under constrained communication and computational resources, making LoRA particularly important for efficient model adaptation. However, directly applying LoRA in FL can still incur substantial communication overhead, particularly in wireless environments. To address this, we propose a novel framework, called Federated LoRA with Structural Sparsification (FLR-SS), which reduces communication cost by sparsifying LoRA matrices through the removal of rows and columns with the smallest norms, thereby preserving the most informative components. We further provide a theoretical convergence analysis of FLR SS and formulate the selection of rows and columns as a bi convex optimization problem, which can be solved efficiently. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that FLR-SS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy improvements of 1.66% to 8.63% while reducing communication traffic by 21.42% to 53.33%.
10.1109/tkde.2026.3752869: Cross-Domain Recommendation (CDR) effectively alleviates the data sparsity problem by transferring knowledge from source domains to target domains. To address growing data privacy concerns, Federated Learning (FL) has been incorporated into CDR, enabling multiple clients to collaborate without exposing raw data. However, most existing federated CDR methods still rely on overlapping entities to bridge different clients. Under strict privacy constraints, such correspondences are often unavailable, causing structural misalignment across isolated clients and weakening cross-domain knowledge transfer. To address this problem, we propose DFTCDR, aDecomposedFederatedTransfer framework forCross-DomainRecommendation. DFTCDR performs cluster-level structural alignment across disjoint domains through complementary modeling of transferable cluster-level structures and local residual interaction patterns. Specifically, we employ PARAFAC2-based tensor decomposition to learn transferable cluster-level structural prototypes, which act as virtual anchors for mapping isolated clients into a shared structural space. To balance transferability and personalization, DFTCDR further models local residual information through intra-domain graph propagation. In addition, a consistency-aware knowledge filtering mechanism evaluates whether each global prototype is consistent with the client local interaction semantics and retains only locally consistent prototypes to mitigate negative transfer. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that DFTCDR outperforms baselines without relying on overlapping entities. Additional experiments demonstrate its overall effectiveness and domain sparsity robustness.
10.1109/tpds.2026.3752125: Next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) applications increasingly span across autonomous administrative entities, necessitating silo-cooperative scheduling to leverage diverse computational resources while preserving data privacy. However, realizing efficient cooperation faces significant challenges arising from infrastructure heterogeneity, Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) workload shifts, and the inherent risks of adversarial environments. Existing approaches, relying predominantly on centralized coordination or independent learning, fail to address the incompatibility of state-action spaces across heterogeneous silos and lack robustness against malicious attacks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeFRiS, a Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning framework for robust and scalable Silo-cooperative IoT application scheduling. DeFRiS integrates three synergistic innovations: (i) an action-space-agnostic policy utilizing candidate resource scoring to enable seamless knowledge transfer across heterogeneous silos; (ii) a silo-optimized local learning mechanism combining Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with clipped policy updates to resolve sparse delayed reward challenges; and (iii) a Dual-Track Non-IID robust decentralized aggregation protocol leveraging gradient fingerprints for similarity-aware knowledge transfer and anomaly detection, and gradient tracking for optimization momentum. Extensive experiments on a distributed testbed with 20 heterogeneous silos and realistic IoT workloads demonstrate that DeFRiS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, DeFRiS reduces average response time by 6.4% and energy consumption by 7.2% compared to the best-performing baseline, while lowering tail latency risk (CVaR$_{0.95}$) by 10.4% and achieving near-zero deadline violations. Furthermore, extensive experiments reveal that DeFRiS achieves over 3 times better performance retention as the system scales and over 8 times better stability in adversarial environments compared to the best-performing baseline.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3751990: The space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) is expected to support ubiquitous edge intelligence in sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks, where federated learning (FL) can exploit distributed data without exposing raw samples. In SAGIN, resource-constrained ground devices and heterogeneous wireless links make synchronous FL vulnerable to stragglers, which may cause excessive training delay. A naive attempt to reduce this delay by excluding straggling devices can introduce distribution drift under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, especially when these devices contain rare or complementary samples. To address these coupled latency and robustness issues, this paper proposes a hierarchical split federated learning (HSFL) framework for SAGIN. In this framework, ground devices execute shallow model layers, Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (AAVs) process the remaining layers and perform edge aggregation, and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites conduct satellite-level aggregation. We derive a convergence upper bound to capture the effects of split layer selection, user association, and data distribution on convergence. A joint optimization problem is formulated to minimize training delay by optimizing split layer selection, device-AAV association, AAV-LEO association, and communication and computing resource allocation. To solve this mixed-integer nonlinear problem, we first design a tabu-assisted block coordinate descent (TA-BCD) algorithm that alternately updates topology association, resource allocation, and split layer selection. We further develop a robust device-admission extension of TA-BCD (RDA-TA-BCD), which jointly optimizes device admission, topology association, and resource scheduling and incorporates federated unlearning to approximately remove the historical model influence of excluded devices. The resulting scheduler protects data-critical bottleneck devices while removing redundant ones, thereby balancing delay reduction with model robustness. Simulation results on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that the proposed algorithms reduce training delay while maintaining model accuracy under heterogeneous SAGIN and non-IID data settings.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3751908: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a compelling paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed machine learning, allowing multiple clients to collaboratively train a global model by transmitting locally computed gradients to a central server without exposing their private data. Nonetheless, recent studies find that the gradients exchanged in the FL system are also vulnerable to privacy leakage, e.g., an attacker can invert shared gradients to reconstruct sensitive data by leveraging pre-trained generative adversarial networks (GAN) as prior knowledge. However, existing attacks simply perform gradient inversion in the latent space of the GAN model, which limits their expression ability and generalizability. To tackle these challenges, we propose Gradient Inversion over Feature Domains (GIFD), which disassembles the GAN model and searches the hierarchical features of the intermediate layers. Instead of optimizing only over the initial latent code, we progressively change the optimized layer, from the initial latent space to intermediate layers closer to the output images. In addition, we design a regularizer to avoid unreal image generation by adding a small ${l_{1}}$ ball constraint to the searching range. We also extend GIFD to the out-of-distribution (OOD) setting, which weakens the assumption that the training sets of GANs and FL tasks obey the same data distribution. Furthermore, we consider the challenging OOD scenario of label inconsistency and propose a label mapping technique as an effective solution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method can achieve high-quality reconstruction and outperform competitive baselines across a variety of FL scenarios.
10.1109/tits.2026.3740049: Transportation digital twins (DTs) can support proactive traffic management and operations by maintaining dynamic virtual representations of transportation systems. Developing transportation DTs requires accurate lane-level geometry, which is commonly obtained from static maps or dedicated sensors. However, these sources limit scalability and may fail to reflect changes in roadway configuration in a timely manner. Moreover, transportation DTs rely on large volumes of multi-source data, and centralizing these data across locations raises privacy and communication concerns. To address these limitations, we introduce Geo-ORBIT (Geometrical Operational Roadway Blueprint with Integrated Twin), a decentralized, privacy-aware framework that adapts to geometry changes. Geo-ORBIT combines label-free lane detection from roadside cameras, DT synchronization, and federated meta-learning. Its core model, GeoLane, infers lane geometry from vehicle trajectories without human labels. Meta-GeoLane adapts the detection parameters to each scene, while FedMeta-GeoLane learns a shared adaptation across sites under federated updates that keep raw data local. Geo-ORBIT connects to SUMO and CARLA to render highway scenes and replay traffic, and supports a closed-loop update in which detected changes in lane geometry are propagated to the running simulation. Validated against independent human annotations on real-world data, the detected geometry achieves an error of approximately 3 m, representing nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement over the public map that supervises training. Moreover, FedMeta-GeoLane transfers a single global model across sites without per-site training and reduces per-camera communication by more than 99% relative to centralizing trajectories. The framework is publicly available athttps://github.com/raynbowy23/FedMeta-GeoLane.git
10.1109/tnse.2026.3750978: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) anomaly detection faces significant challenges due to dynamic network topologies, non-IID data distributions, high-dimensional multi-modal features, and privacy preservation. Conventional federated learning (FL) approaches suffer from high communication overhead, poor adaptation to concept drift, and difficulty in preserving cross-modal correlations. To address these limitations, we propose a dynamic federated learning (DFL) framework that integrates attention-based generative anomaly detection with tensorized aggregation. Client-side multi-modal statistics, including detection losses, KL divergence, attention distributions, PCA features, and metadata, are unified into a six-mode tensor on the server, which is incrementally updated via incremental tensor-train decomposition (ITTD). This enables efficient updates, preserves structural correlations across modalities, and provides explicit monitoring of drift through rank variation and reconstruction error. A hard-soft coupled decision mechanism further selects and weights client updates by combining adaptive thresholding, latent-space clustering, and variance-aware weighting. Experimental results demonstrate that on the IoT-23 dataset, our method achieves an F1 score of 95.89% with a reduced false positive rate (FPR) of 1.58%, while on the SECOM manufacturing dataset it attains 95.02% F1 with 2.04% FPR under the full tensorized DFL setting. Moreover, the proposed DFL with tensor aggregation reduces communication overhead compared with baseline FL methods, indicating its potential to enable scalable, privacy-preserving anomaly detection in dynamic IIoT environments.
10.1109/tifs.2026.3751573: Federated Graph Learning (FGL) has garnered increasing interest thanks to its ability to harness the representational power of graphs, while its development is still impeded by privacy issues stemming from the direct upload of a participant’s local model. In this study, we address privacy concerns of FGL by Differential Privacy (DP), and devise a novel graph-level framework for Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning with Differential Privacy (DP-HFGL). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to investigate graph-level classification tasks in federated setting, while providing rigorous DP guarantee. The primary challenges in this work stem from the intra-client feature and structure heterogeneity among graphs, inter-client statistical heterogeneity in local distribution shifts and DP-required noise injection. Specifically, these factors bring significant variance to the model gradients, leading to unstable training and utility degradation. To address these issues, DP-HFGL applies a dual-channel model to process feature and structure information separately and shares only structural information with the server, which significantly mitigates the impact of heterogeneity under noise perturbation. To further enhance the overall performance, we perform DP operations only on the shared structure knowledge to naturally reduce the norm of local updates before clipping, making local updates adaptive to the DP operations.
