Extensive experiments on several types of datasets, including Molecules, Proteins, Social Networks and Computer Vision, demonstrate the effectiveness of DP-HFGL in federated graph learning.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3751775: This paper presents an invariant federated learning framework for resource-constrained edge intelligence. The framework first identifies and excludes low-value or aberrant clients, and then enforces model-level invariance to preserve generalization. Motivated by pretraining-based client valuation, we show that some clients may have negligible or even detrimental contributions to global aggregation under severe heterogeneity or asynchrony. Accordingly, we propose a practical exit strategy based on client utility and delay, which removes such clients from the main training loop to protect in-distribution (ID) performance. To maintain robust performance for excluded and resource-constrained clients, we introduce FedIPG (Federated Learning with Invariant Penalty for Generalization), which promotes approximate orthogonality between invariant and heterogeneous parameter components through a gradient-based penalty. We provide theoretical analysis showing that low-value client exit can improve aggregation and that FedIPG tightens an upper bound on out-of-distribution (OOD) risk without increasing communication overhead during formal training. Extensive experiments on four domain-generalization benchmarks and multiple client scales demonstrate that the combined exit + FedIPG framework improves ID accuracy, enhances OOD generalization over recent baselines, and maintains stable convergence. Visualization results further indicate that FedIPG reduces reliance on confounding features and encourages more task-relevant feature usage.
10.1109/tifs.2026.3751579: Federated learning (FL) is vulnerable to multi-vector poisoning attacks that combine clean-label backdoors, gradient manipulation, and Byzantine coordination to evade detection while corrupting model behavior. Existing defenses, limited to single-layer aggregation rules, fail against adaptive, coordinated adversaries. We present HQRL (Hierarchical Quantum Reinforcement Learning), a novel defense framework that employs a multitier quantum reinforcement learning agent, strategic, tactical, and operational, to detect and mitigate coordinated threats dynamically. Each tier utilizes parameterized quantum circuits trained via Quantum Natural Gradient (QNG) with geo-aware Fisher information, enabling rapid adaptation under NISQ-era constraints. HQRL integrates error mitigation and supports secure aggregation for end-to-end privacy. To ensure deployability, we provide a classical fallback controller mirroring HQRL’s decisions, enabling seamless runtime switching and operational continuity when quantum resources are unavailable. Evaluated on CIFAR-10, FEMNIST, and Shakespeare under multi-vector attacks, HQRL improves defense effectiveness by 14.3%, converges 86 rounds faster, and achieves an 87.4% Bayesian probability of superiority over classical hierarchical baselines. Mechanistic analysis shows a significant correlation between entanglement entropy and robustness (r = 0.533, p < 0.001), suggesting quantum-enhanced threat discrimination. HQRL establishes a new paradigm in resilient FL, demonstrating that quantum-enhanced decision-making can effectively counter sophisticated, multistage adversarial campaigns.
10.1109/tcad.2026.3751981: Gang scheduling is becoming increasingly important in real-time AI and accelerator-driven systems, where work-loads execute in parallel on multiple processing units. Motivated by real-time DNN inference workloads with parallelism-dependent execution times, this paper introduces configurable non-preemptive gang (cNPG) tasks as an abstraction that captures their key execution characteristics. It proposes a strict partitioning framework for scheduling real-time cNPG tasks that jointly determines task parallelism levels, processor partitions, and task assignments. By enforcing a uniform parallelism level within each partition, the framework eliminates cross-partition interference and enables schedulability analysis using well-understood uniprocessor techniques. To solve the resulting offline design problem, this paper introduces Pruned Adaptive Beam Search (PABS), a search-based heuristic that explores partitioning and parallelism assignments while pruning unpromising partial solutions. Evaluations with large-scale synthetic workloads and real-world Edge TPU benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves a higher schedulability ratio than the state-of-the-art global and federated gang scheduling techniques, as well as a previous strict partitioning heuristic.
10.1109/twc.2026.3751427: Beamforming coordination is critical to interference mitigation in full frequency reuse (FFR) multi-satellite systems, thereby enhancing spectral efficiency. However, existing optimization-based and learning-based beamforming methods face significant challenges in satellite networks due to the rapidly changing spatiotemporal relationships and constrained on-board computational resources. In this paper, we propose a cross-task joint satellite selection and beamforming adaptation framework based on federated meta-reinforcement learning (FedMRL), with lightweight and generalizable capabilities in distributed multi-satellite networks. Specifically, a Meta-Critic network is pretrained on distributed multi-task channel state information (CSI) datasets , and then guides the satellite selection and beamforming design for new tasks by transferable meta-knowledge. An online meta-knowledge update mechanism is designed to enhance adaptability to new scenarios, which incorporates federated aggregation to continuously refine the meta-knowledge based on decentralized experiences. To further reduce the signaling overhead in the collaborative process, we integrate a dual-loss knowledge distillation (KD) module into the FedMRL framework, achieving substantial parameter reduction with minimal performance degradation. Simulation results demonstrate the superior cross-task applicability and computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm over baseline schemes.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3751266: The growing scale of deep models is straining learning at the edge: resource-constrained devices struggle to train locally, and heterogeneous wireless links create communication bottlenecks, resulting in stragglers. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose a multi-edge split federated learning (MESFL) framework, which facilitates split federated learning (SFL) over a mobile edge computing (MEC) system. The MEC system comprises client devices, edge servers, and a federated (fed) server. Server-side sub-model aggregation is performed on each edge server. The periodic federated aggregation is performed on the fed server. We consider a practical resource-limited scenario where all client devices and edge servers have limited computation and memory capacities. The proposed MESFL framework jointly optimizes sub-model offloading decisions, layer splitting, and federated aggregation frequency to improve the learning efficiency. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem to minimize the learning convergence bound subject to latency and memory constraints. The problem is NP-hard, and we apply an exact finite-interval decomposition with interval-level pruning, which yields a globally optimal solution when the fixed-interval subproblems are solved to optimality, or a certified anytime solution under a time limit. Extensive experiments on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 datasets with ResNet-18, together with an architecture study on CIFAR-10 using VGG-11 and MobileNetV2, validate the effectiveness of the proposed MESFL framework. We compare MESFL with seven baseline methods in terms of test accuracy and training latency. We further conduct an ablation analysis to study the effects of offloading and layer splitting decisions.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3750980: Personalized federated learning (PFL) addresses statistical heterogeneity by adapting models to individual clients, but its utility can degrade substantially under client-level differential privacy (DP). Two major causes are rigid parameter partitioning and isotropic update clipping, which overlook the continuous importance distribution and distinct optimization roles of model parameters. We propose FedVPC, a privacy-preserving PFL framework consisting of two complementary components. First, the Variable Hierarchical Pyramid (VHP) uses an empirical diagonal Fisher proxy to softly stratify parameters into personalized, bridging, and globally aligned groups. Second, the Parameter-Customized Constraint (PCC) applies group-aware regularization before client-level clipping and Gaussian perturbation to reduce optimization distortion. We establish a client-level DP guarantee through update clipping, distributed Gaussian perturbation, and RDP accounting, while secure aggregation restricts the server to aggregate-only observation. We also characterize convergence under heterogeneous data. Experiments on five datasets show that FedVPC consistently outperforms representative DP-FL and DP-PFL baselines, with improvements of up to 7.66 percentage points across the evaluated settings. FedVPC also demonstrates robustness to data heterogeneity, client scale, and model architecture while showing empirical resistance to gradient inversion under the evaluated diagnostic setting.
10.1109/tcsvt.2026.3750827: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without exposing raw data, thus ensuring privacy compliance. However, data heterogeneity among participants introduces significant challenges for effective federated optimization. While prior research has attempted to address this issue typically by regularizing local updates or fine-tuning the global model, the aggregation weights in most FL frameworks are still determined solely by dataset size. This simplistic strategy may hinder convergence and limit overall model effectiveness, highlighting the ongoing need for adaptive and secure aggregation methods. This paper proposes FedAED, a novel FL framework that Adaptively adjusts aggregation weights through Editing Directions derived from client model updates. The editing direction vector encodes the semantic trajectory of local model updates, effectively capturing the underlying data heterogeneity across clients. This approach enables more accurate aggregation that is well aligned with global optimization goals, preserves privacy, and requires no auxiliary data. As a result, FedAED enhances both the stability and generalization ability of the global model. Comprehensive experimental results confirm that our approach consistently surpasses strong baselines and significantly improves the effectiveness of FL under heterogeneous environments.
10.1109/tifs.2026.3750716: This paper studies a novel quantum federated learning (QFL) framework that leverages inherent quantum noise to enforce differential privacy (DP) and protect model updates from information leakage in current near-term quantum devices. Specifically, we achieve targeted DP guarantees during model training by (i) varying the number of measurement shots, and (ii) leveraging unavoidable depolarizing channel noise. To adapt privacy levels based on varying training conditions, we further introduce an adaptive DP strategy using a multi-armed bandit (MAB) agent at each quantum device, enabling dynamic control over the trade-off between privacy and model performance. Moreover, we present a rigorous convergence analysis of our proposed QFL-DP model. Our theoretical analysis and numerical evaluation reveal the following key properties: i) the global QFL-DP model converges to a bounded error floor, which indicates that, despite leveraging inherent quantum noise for DP, the model’s performance remains stable, making our approach suitable for real-world QFL applications; ii) a clear trade-off exists between privacy guarantees and model accuracy, and the adaptive MAB strategy further enhances this trade-off by enabling adaptive privacy budgeting with efficient noise allocation based on training dynamics and client needs; iii) our theoretical results are consistent with simulations, thereby demonstrating the superiority of the proposed framework over baseline approaches in terms of training accuracy, adaptive privacy preservation, and robustness against adversarial examples. Overall, the results highlight a tunable trade-off between privacy and robustness, offering an efficient and secure QFL solution for current nearterm quantum devices.
10.1109/tifs.2026.3750691: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without directly sharing data, thereby offering effective privacy guarantees. However, the decentralized architecture of FL makes it vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where adversaries can compromise a subset of clients to inject malicious updates, causing the global model to misbehave on specific trigger inputs. The existing defenses typically rely on static rules or auxiliary validation data, which often lack adaptability against evolving attack strategies or introduce privacy risks and computational overhead. To address these challenges, we propose GameRLFed, a robust defense framework that formulates the FL security problem as a repeated game with incomplete information. Without requiring any auxiliary data, the server infers the malicious tendencies of each client based on current updates and historical observations and employs reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the aggregation weights for mitigating backdoor effects. Moreover, attackers adaptively evolve their strategies in response to the behavior of the server to maximize the effectiveness of their attacks while minimizing the risk of detection, resulting in complex game interactions. Theoretically, we prove that GameRLFed can converge to a near-optimal global model under adversarial dynamics. Extensive experiments conducted across multiple datasets and attack types show that GameRLFed outperforms six baseline methods in terms of robustness, adaptability, and computational efficiency.
10.1109/tmlcn.2026.3750808: The paradigm shift towards Softwarized Edge Computing (SEC) and 6G networks necessitates the deployment of deep learning models as flexible, lightweight Virtual Network Functions (VNFs). However, training high-performance Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in such resource-constrained, heterogeneous environments presents significant challenges. Existing low-rank adaptation methods often rely on static rank allocations or require heavy pre-trained backbones, limiting their applicability for training from scratch or adapting to novel edge domains. In this paper, we propose GILoRaT++, a unified framework for resource-efficient training and fine-tuning. We introduce a novelRank Demand Score, grounded in gradient sensitivity analysis, to replace global greedy heuristics. This metric allows the network to autonomously identify layer-wise capacity bottlenecks, incrementing the rank of specific layers only when their sensitivity to the loss function dictates necessity. Furthermore, we propose GILoRaFT, a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) strategy that combines aggressive SVD-based compression with feature distillation and weight perturbation control to adapt models with minimal parameter overhead. Finally, we address the challenge of Federated Learning (FL) in heterogeneous edge environments with a case study. We propose a budget-constrained rank allocation scheme and solve the low-rank rotational ambiguity problem using Orthogonal Procrustes Alignment. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Brain Tumor MRI datasets demonstrate that GILoRAT++ achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with up to 20× parameter reduction compared to full-rank baselines, while offering superior convergence speed in federated settings.
10.1109/tcc.2026.3741038: Statistical heterogeneity in 6 G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks severely limits standard federated learning paradigms, leading to significant weight divergence and suboptimal personalization. We proposed ACPFL-KD, an adaptive clustering personalized federated learning framework that synthesizes dynamic topology reconstruction with data-free, duallayer knowledge distillation. Diverging from static clustering regimes and conventional federated distillation, our Affinity Propagation strategy leverages lightweight feature representations and a theoretically grounded, regularized similarity metric to autonomously restructure the network topology without predefined cluster constraints, even with sparse client participation. We devise a synergistic dual-layer knowledge-sharing architecture to stabilize convergence. At the intra-cluster level, coordinatewise median aggregation yields robust teacher models that guide clients in extracting group consensus; simultaneously, an inter-cluster adaptive regularization strategy fuses heterogeneous knowledge increments to effectively bridge information silos. Experiments on five datasets, including the real-world autonomous driving dataset BDD100 K, together with rigorous theoretical convergence analysis, validate this framework. In highly non- IID settings, ACPFL-KD consistently outperforms state-of-theart personalization and distillation baselines (e.g., Fed-DFA, FedPer), achieving superior classification accuracy, particularly in complex mobility scenarios. Furthermore, it maintains this lead while demonstrating accelerated convergence and drastically reducing central communication bandwidth overhead compared to current baselines. Future work will explore cross-domain adaptation to further enhance scalability in dynamic, real-world deployments.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3750240: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving traffic perception in roadside unit (RSU)-assisted cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) networks, but vehicle deletion requires removing both historical model influence and subsequent communication participation. In cell-free C-V2X, deletion further affects aggregation, RSU association, vehicle-to-RSU (V2R) transmission, and energy accounting. We propose traffic context-directed Fisher corrective unlearning (TC-FCU), which uses a diagonal empirical-Fisher preconditioner and momentum-stabilized updates for low-cost corrective retraining with traffic-context-adaptive correction. We further formulate machine unlearning (MU) execution as deletion scheduling under deadline and processing-capacity constraints, jointly considering pre-deletion resource consumption, corrective unlearning cost, and the marginal network-side energy change of the remaining vehicles. We analyze the Fisher–Hessian relation under explicit assumptions, local descent, and deletion-cost monotonicity. Simulations show that TC-FCU approaches full-retraining forgetting quality with much lower runtime, while Proposed Timing reduces normalized cost over benchmark scheduling schemes.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3749663: Federated edge learning (FEL) has significant advantages in terms of protecting user privacy and reducing communication overhead in vehicular networks. Improving learning accuracy and minimizing communication overhead by adjusting resource allocation strategies is the research focus of FEL. Although FEL helps enhance privacy through data encryption, information leakage caused by localization errors remains a challenging problem. To address this issue, we utilize the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to calculate the vehicle localization errors, filter out vehicles that meet the localization accuracy requirements, and then select vehicles from them to participate in FEL. Furthermore, a joint optimization problem for dynamic resource allocation is proposed, in order to balance the learning accuracy and communication overhead. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP). To solve such MDP, we adopt a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based approach and propose a novel CRLB-based FEL algorithm, i.e., FC-TD3,which structurally integrates a reliability-filtering mechanism into the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) framework. By employing this mechanism, the algorithm dynamically constructs a high-confidence candidate pool to select vehicles that meet localization accuracy requirements, thereby ensuring that only reliable agents participate in the FEL process. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional algorithms in dealing with such problems. Finally, we conduct simulations to validate the performance of the algorithm and clarify the impact of different parameters on system performance through numerical analysis.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3748952: Federated learning (FL) trains a shared model across distributed clients without centralizing their data. Its open participation exposes aggregation to model-poisoning and Byzantine attacks, so the server must admit only updates that advance the shared objective. Existing defenses rely on protocol level authentication or statistical robustness. Neither evaluates whether an admitted update moves the global model along the task-induced descent direction. Under non-IID data and partial participation, authenticated and statistically plausible updates can jointly push training off task. We introduce SATF (Selective Admission via Task-directional Filtering), a server-side admission mechanism. SATF ranks updates by their directional alignment with a round-wise reference direction and applies an interquartile-range gate on update magnitudes. It needs no trusted dataset and does not use the Byzantine fraction as an algorithmic input. We bound the adversarial perturbation of the reference direction and give a worst-case benign-majority bound for the retained set, extended to the accepted set under a stated gate condition. We derive a one-step descent bound and a sublinear multi-round convergence rate up to an explicit Byzantine-dependent bias term, and we characterize the scaling detection threshold of the magnitude gate. On Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 with one hundred clients and three random seeds, against FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, FLAME-Clip, FLTrust, and Multi-Krum, SATF, at moderate heterogeneity, attains the highest mean accuracy under strong-replacement attacks on CIFAR-10 and stays within two points of the best method under strong replacement on Fashion-MNIST and under mixed attacks on both datasets. We also report its limitations under high heterogeneity and scaling attacks.
10.1109/tce.2026.3749446: The rapid growth of consumer electronics (CE) systems introduces significant challenges for Federated Learning (FL), particularly in managing device heterogeneity, ensuring data privacy, and achieving personalized model adaptation. However, existing FL methods often struggle to adequately capture complex multi-level relationships or effectively balance global knowledge sharing with nuanced local adaptation, particularly with heterogeneous consumer devices and user-specific service contexts. In this paper, we propose a Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) framework with Large Language Model (LLM)-Guided Graph Representation, named PFL-LLMGR, to model intricate cross-device semantic relationships, facilitate multilevel collaboration, and achieve refined personalization without sharing raw data in an end-edge-cloud architecture. Specifically, an LLM is incorporated to analyze lightweight device metadata on the cloud, so as to guide global graph pruning and node fusion while capturing deeper semantic relationships. A local subgraph construction scheme based on multi-source information fusion is then introduced on the edge, and an edge-deployed Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is trained to fuse features within these subgraphs, generating enhanced representations distributed back to clients. Furthermore, local models are decomposed into feature extractors that participate in edge aggregation and personalized classifiers that remain on clients. An alternating training scheme is developed to synchronize local model training based on edge-fused features while GCN parameters are fixed, and update the edge GCN using client-side feedback while local parameters are fixed, effectively balancing shared knowledge and local adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-10, DIGIT, and the CE-oriented Office-Home benchmark demonstrate that PFL-LLMGR achieves consistently competitive and often superior accuracy under label heterogeneity, domain shift, and varying client scales, with an improvement of up to 2.65 percentage points over the strongest baseline on Office-Home withK= 50, offering valuable insights for advanced FL in consumer electronics systems, especially in enhancing collaborative intelligence and personalization.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3749791: Federated Learning (FL) allows collaborative training with local gradients uploaded by clients instead of sharing their raw data. For scenarios like the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) where large volumes of sensitive driving data are generated, cryptography techniques are leveraged to encrypt or mask the local gradients. However, these privacy-preserving approaches are vulnerable to poisoning attacks, as it is difficult to detect malicious gradients within the ciphertext. Potential poisoning attacks in IoVs can significantly impact the accuracy and performance of the system. To combat this issue, we propose PAFL, a privacy-awareness and adversarial-resilient FL model. At the heart of our method is an aggregation mechanism delicately designed to protect private data while being robust against poisoning attacks. During the aggregation process, self mask and gradient mask are devised on the original gradient to prevent privacy leakage. Furthermore, an evaluation mechanism is implemented to identify and filter out malicious vehicles from subsequent model updates, ultimately defending against poisoning attacks. Our model suits the characteristics of IoVs, reducing the communication overhead from$O(n^{2})$to approximately$O(nlogn)$, while effectively mitigating poisoning attacks and safeguarding privacy. Experiments have validated the effectiveness and feasibility of PAFL in large-scale IoVs, which outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by reducing the aggregation time by nearly 8 times.
10.1109/tase.2026.3749430: While numerous machine learning approaches have been proposed for machine remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, they typically rely on centralized datasets for model training. In real-world scenarios, however, obtaining these datasets is often impractical, since machine monitoring data (e.g., from aircraft engines) is proprietary to various stakeholders (e.g., airline companies) and cannot be freely shared. Federated learning (FL) offers a promising solution by enabling collaborative training of a global model without requiring direct data sharing. However, federated RUL prediction models often face performance degradation due to the decentralized and non-uniform distribution of training data. Recently, large language models (LLMs) pretrained on web-scale datasets have demonstrated strong generalization capability in representation learning, suggesting their potential to provide shared representations for mitigating data heterogeneity in federated RUL prediction. Specifically, frozen prompt embeddings provide a shared external target representation over RUL labels. This fixed representation serves as a partially ordinal regularizer that encourages compatible feature learning across clients with heterogeneous local data. In this paper, we propose FedLER, a novel framework that enhances federated RUL prediction model training by incorporating frozen LLM-derived prompt embeddings through knowledge distillation. To address the mismatch between the generic embedding space and the specific domains of clients’ local datasets, we further design an alignment module that adapts the embeddings before distillation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedLER significantly improves the performance of federated RUL prediction models under various FL scenarios.
10.1109/tsusc.2026.3749409: Federated cloud–edge computing supports latency sensitive applications but complicates sustainable and SLA aware resource management. Existing schedulers usually treat energy, carbon emissions, renewable energy, battery storage, and SLA compliance separately and therefore miss the interactions among them. This paper presents a unified mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for task scheduling in federated cloud–edge systems. The formulation jointly models tier specific power profiles, renewable generation, battery charging and discharging, task migration, grid carbon emissions, and contention-aware SLA penalties. We evaluate it on workloads derived from Google Cluster Traces v3 and compare exact MILP optimization with the NSGA-II evolutionary algorithm and two greedy baselines. In the main setting, MILP produces 2.7 times fewer SLA violations than NSGA-II while using less energy, and on-site renewable supply reduces grid carbon emissions by 44.6% relative to grid-only operation. A scalability study shows that MILP suits offline planning for moderate instance sizes, whereas NSGA-II offers more predictable runtime for larger online instances.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3748545: Model heterogeneity poses a significant challenge in Heterogeneous Federated Learning (HtFL). In scenarios with diverse model architectures, directly aggregating model parameters is impractical, leading HtFL methods to incorporate an extra guiding objective alongside the original local objective on each client to facilitate collaboration. However, this often results in a mismatch between the guiding and local objectives. To resolve this mismatch and ensure the guiding objective consistently benefits each client's original objective rather than interfering with it, we propose Federated Learning-to-Guide (FedL2G), a federated method that adaptively learns to guide local training in a meta-learning manner. In this way, the client can learn the necessary knowledge from the process of aligning globally shared information, thereby compensating for the required information for its local task. We theoretically prove that FedL2G achieves a non-convex convergence rate of $\mathcal {O}(1/T)$. We also conduct extensive experiments across three types of data heterogeneity and six model heterogeneity settings, using 14 heterogeneous model architectures (e.g., CNNs and ViTs). The results show that FedL2G consistently outperforms 12 state-of-the-art methods in terms of test accuracy (both in-distribution and out-of-distribution) as well as communication and computational overhead, across standard benchmark datasets and specialized medical scenarios.
10.1109/tnsm.2026.3748922: Existing AI-based intrusion detection systems are typically trained for specific network environments, leading to significant performance degradation when deployed in different settings or exposed to evolving attack strategies. We propose GRIDS (Generalized Representation-based Intrusion Detection System), a federated contrastive learning framework for cross-environment intrusion detection that keeps raw traffic data local. GRIDS employs a Transformer-based encoder trained with supervised contrastive learning across distributed network environments, learning a shared representation without exchanging sensitive traffic data. The encoder embeds network flow features into a latent space where semantically similar traffic patterns cluster together, enabling effective anomaly detection via k-nearest neighbor scoring. Evaluated on four heterogeneous NetFlow datasets, GRIDS outperforms existing federated IDS baselines on average with a single unified model. In leave-one-out cross-validation, a substantial portion of the detection capability of GRIDS transfers to network environments unseen during training, and the level of transfer varies across target networks. Deployment at such a network requires no labeled attack data or fine-tuning. It uses the benign traffic of the network as the kNN reference set and its unlabeled traffic for normalization and threshold calibration. The framework targets deployments in which a single model protects multiple heterogeneous networks.
10.1109/tgcn.2026.3748550: Existing particle-based Bayesian federated learning algorithms face challenges in substantial maintenance expenses in terms of computation, storage, and communication of particles, as well as the oversight of inherent correlation among particles in the lower layers of network parameters. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose a federated low-rank Bayesian approximation learning algorithm via Stein variational gradient descent (FedLoBA) in this paper. Specifically, we verify the occurrence of low-rank subspace among parameters in the same layer of particles through experiment and then design a low-rank Bayesian approximation module to decrease the maintenance costs and improve the shareability among particles. The lower and upper bounds of the discrepancy between the original and approximate posterior distributions are established theoretically. Furthermore, an aggregation refinement strategy has been developed to eliminate extra cross terms during the particle aggregation stage. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FedLoBA algorithm exhibits superior prediction accuracy compared to other benchmark algorithms, as well as significant efficiency advantages in terms of computation, storage, and communication over its full-dimensional competitor.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3748974: The growing use of large pre-trained models in edge computing has made model inference on mobile clients both feasible and popular. Yet these devices remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks, threatening model robustness and security. Federated adversarial training (FAT) offers a promising solution by enhancing robustness while preserving client privacy. However, FAT often yields a generalized global model that struggles with heterogeneous client data, leading to limited personalization and significant communication overhead, while largely overlooking robustness against Byzantine adversarial clients. In this paper, we propose Lorica, a personalized synergistic adversarial training framework that delivers customized defense models through a two-phase process. In Phase 1, Lorica applies LoRA-FA for local adversarial fine-tuning, enabling personalized robustness while reducing communication by uploading only LoRA-FA parameters. In Phase 2, a forward-gating selection strategy improves benign accuracy, further refining the personalized model. This yields tailored defense models that effectively balance robustness and accuracy. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Lorica can achieve up to 68× improvements in communication efficiency compared to state-of-the-art algorithms, while achieving up to 35.3% and 55.0% enhancements in adversarial robustness and benign accuracy, respectively.
10.1109/tcomm.2026.3747879: This paper investigates age-of-information (AoI) aware federated learning over wireless networks with finite speed pinching antennas. In contrast to existing studies that assume an infinitely high antenna moving speed, a practical round based training procedure is considered, where the pinching antenna is repositioned during the local training phase and its feasible movement range depends on the selected devices. This creates a new coupling among device selection, antenna placement, local training time, model uploading time, and AoI evolution. To characterize the impact of antenna moving speed, the rate gain over the fixed antenna and the gap to the infinite speed benchmark are analyzed. Subsequently, an overall AoI minimization problem is formulated under a round latency deadline by jointly optimizing the selected device set and the pinching antenna position. A coalitional game based device selection algorithm is proposed, where finite speed antenna placement is incorporated into the coalition utility evaluation. For antenna placement, the optimal search region is derived by exploiting the mobility constraint and device location span, based on which a branch-and-bound (BnB) algorithm is developed to obtain the global optimum. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can accelerate learning convergence, reduce the sum AoI, and improve device participation compared with baseline schemes, demonstrating the potential of pinching antennas for enhancing federated learning through flexible spatial reconfiguration.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3748054: Federated continual learning (FCL) has attracted considerable interest by enabling local clients to continually acquire knowledge from new tasks. However, most FCL methods assume that the global server has prior knowledge of the arrival times and number of categories for new tasks, which is unrealistic in the real world. Furthermore, they neglect the importance of positive inter-task semantic relationships when learning new tasks and are significantly affected by irrelevant relationships from old tasks, thereby exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To resolve the above challenges, we develop a novelTaskRelevance-drivenPromptExpansion (TRPE) model. Specifically, to eliminate the reliance on prior knowledge of new tasks, we propose an out-of-distribution detector to identify the arrival of new tasks within local clients, along with a radius-adaptive DBSCAN to infer the quantity of categories in new tasks on the proxy server. Moreover, to explore positive inter-task relationships, we calculate the affinity between the original gradient for learning new task and its gradient orthogonal to the feature space of old tasks to evaluate semantic relevance between old and new tasks from a global perspective. Then, we use this global task relevance to determine the key-prompt pair for new tasks and identify highly related old tasks. After concatenating their prompts for training, we can leverage such positive inter-task relations to improve the continual learning of newly arriving tasks. To balance the learning of new tasks and the forgetting of old ones, a soft orthogonality constraint is applied to the local key and prompt gradients. Experiments spanning diverse datasets and backbones confirm the efficacy of our TRPE model.
10.1109/tce.2026.3747875: We present FedGuard-XAI, a novel federated learning (FL) framework for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments, combining Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with SHAP-based explainability and gradient-based adversarial defense mechanisms for breast cancer detection. Our approach addresses the critical challenges of data privacy, model robustness, and clinical interpretability in cross-continental healthcare settings where sensitive medical imaging data must remain decentralized across distributed IoMT devices and institutional networks. We evaluated FedGuard-XAI using a private dataset of 8,220 mammograms from South Asian populations (collected from five tertiary hospitals in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh) combined with public datasets including TCGA-BRCA (1,098 patients), CBIS-DDSM (2,620 cases), and INbreast (410 images). The FL framework incorporates a novel Differential Privacy-Preserving Attention Mechanism (DP-PAM) achieving 94.3% accuracy while maintaining ε = 2.1 privacy guarantee. Building on this privacy foundation, adversarial robustness was evaluated against FGSM, PGD, and C&W attacks, retaining 86.4% average accuracy across all attack settings (a 7.9 percentage-point degradation), compared with 51.5–71.0 points for baseline models. The framework’s explainability module identified candidate biomarkers in South Asian populations, suggesting distinct tissue density patterns that warrant further clinical validation, while enabling secure collaborative learning across geographically distributed IoMT healthcare systems without centralizing sensitive patient data. Clinical validation with radiologists across three experience levels demonstrated 7.4% diagnostic accuracy improvement and 31% reduction in evaluation time, establishing FedGuard-XAI as a practical solution for privacy-preserving, robust, and interpretable AI deployment in real-world IoMT-enabled healthcare environments.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3748286: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the open and broadcast nature of wireless links such as 5G/6G have made user privacy a critical issue. The complex and dynamic channel environments can degrade communication performance as well as covert transmission. Therefore, this paper proposes an intelligent evaluation algorithm for covert transmission and performance based on federated learning (FL) and a Gramba Neural Network. First, a covert communication model assisted by intelligent reconfigurable surface (IRS) and artificial noise (AN) is established considering N-Nakagami fading channels. IRS is employed to reshape the propagation environment, and AN is used to disrupt signal detection. This model employs hierarchical FL with client-edge-cloud layers to protect data privacy. Edge computing is employed to reduce cloud communication overhead while adapting to data heterogeneity. This also improves privacy protection and mitigates overfitting. The Gramba neural network employs SpatSAGE, which is a spatial domain multi-hop weighted graph convolutional network with hop-interaction, for local feature extraction. A graph-aware MambaMixer is used to improve modeling of long-range dependencies. It integrates a structure-aware attention mechanism to better capture complex topological structures. Two datasets based on covert throughput (CT) and detection error probability (DEP) are generated for performance evaluation. Simulation results are presented that demonstrate superior evaluation performance compared to the GraphSAGE, GraphMamba, GAT, Graphormer and Gramba models. FL-Gramba achieves mean squared error reductions of 17.3% and 16.9% over GraphMamba with the two datasets.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3748036: With the rapid development of vehicular network technology, vehicles can obtain entertainment/safety information services through V2V and V2I communication. Vehicular intrusion detection systems (VIDSs) are essential for protecting vehicles against cyberattacks. Existing deep neural networkbased VIDSs have achieved better results in detecting malicious attack traffic. However, most systems rarely account for performance differences among vehicles, such as their computational and storage resources. In particular, the performance difference between older and the latest smart vehicles is more obvious. To accommodate vehicles with different performance levels, a twostage VIDS training framework based on federated knowledge distillation is proposed, which simultaneously produces two types of detection models: 1) a complex model and 2) a lightweight model. In the first stage, considering the distributed characteristics of the Internet of Vehicles, we designed a federated learning algorithm based on representative clients and learning quality to train complex models. This algorithm enhances the detection capability of complex models by selecting optimal model parameters. In the second stage, we design a progressive knowledge distillation algorithm that adaptively adjusts the distillation temperature to transfer detection knowledge from the complex model to lightweight models with lower resource requirements. Experiments on public datasets show that the proposed federated learning method improves the complex model's class-average accuracy, while progressive distillation enhances the detection performance of lightweight models.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3747836: Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning (FDRL) has been regarded as an emerging paradigm to empower various distributed Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL) in 5G and Beyond. However, a number of approaches fail to jointly take into consideration the limitations of communication resource and energy capacity of Client Devices (CDs) to perform tasks, thereby hindering convergence and degrading overall model accuracy. Therefore, in this paper, we propose SAFL, a novel Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)- Aided FDRL strategy with layer-wise aggregation, to realize energy/communication-efficient FL. To this end, the FL Server (FLS) adopts SWIPT to broadcast the global model to all CDs and simultaneously charges a number of resource-limited CDs for their local training. In order to balance energy/communication resource consumption and FL performance, an improved Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based Actor-Critic with Proximal Policy Optimization (AC-PPO) approach is designed to enable lightweight model uploading, by introducing entropy regularization to achieve the trade-off between action exploration and policy exploitation in DRL for layer-wise model aggregation at the FLS. Furthermore, a double-weight aggregation mechanism is designed to update the global model in an energy/communicationefficient manner. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that SAFL achieves optimized energy consumption and lower communication overhead without sacrificing model accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3748371: Deploying hierarchical federated learning (HFL) in cloud-edge-end collaborative networks has become a mainstream approach for training models without exposing raw data. However, the non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) nature among mobile clients (MCs), compounded by their mobility, remains a structural challenge that HFL cannot circumvent, potentially preventing the global model from reaching target accuracy or substantially increasing the latency to do so. Existing solutions primarily address these challenges from the MC perspective, through implicit data or model fusion, leaving the potential of edge server (ES) collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose an HFL under mobility via model migration (HFL-M3) framework to reduce latency. Before training, it divides the MCs into class-balanced virtual sets, mitigating aggregated gradient bias and reducing the number of cloud rounds required to reach the target accuracy. During training, it dynamically maps the virtual sets to the ESs based on the MCs' current physical access states and migrates the model via the ES topology to control latency per round. Experimental results demonstrate that HFL-M3 achieves an average reduction of 12.68% in rounds and 9.73% in latency compared to benchmark frameworks across various Non-IID settings on three datasets.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3748013: Vertical federated graph neural networks (VFGNNs) have garnered growing attention as a promising technique for intelligent network services, owing to their ability to leverage distributed graph data while preserving data privacy. For any service that prioritizes user security, backdoor attacks are a common security challenge that requires focused assessment. Unlike Euclidean data, the intricate interactions between nodes through links render gradient-based label inference ineffective, which introduces ambiguity to trigger features. As a result, existing backdoor attack strategies designed for vertical federated learning (VFL) encounter challenges when directly applied to graph data. In this study, we investigate the potential of backdoor attacks orchestrated by malicious network participants against VFGNNs. We introduce Graph-Infiltrator, a tailored backdoor attack framework, which incorporates an optional label inference strategy and sophisticated data poisoning techniques tailored for VFGNNs, complemented by a feasible model poisoning strategy. This framework facilitates malicious network participants in executing backdoor attacks against VFGNNs even when the attacker lacks label information while contending with link interference. Experiments show that with no more than 5 labeled samples, the adversary achieves attacks with success rates exceeding 90% in most settings, often reaching 100%, with negligible impact on the primary task. Our proposed approach significantly outperforms existing backdoor attack methods designed for Euclidean data against VFL, unveiling vulnerabilities in VFGNNs.
10.1109/tkde.2026.3748372: Finding dense subgraphs in multilayer graphs is a key problem in graph analytics. In many real-world applications, different providers supply the layers of a multilayer graph subject to privacy policies. These providers must cooperate to detect cohesive subgraphs without revealing their sensitive inputs. This paper studies exact cohesive subgraph mining on multilayer graphs in a federated security environment using secure multi-party computation (SMPC), with the goals of minimizing costly SMPC operations and limiting sensitive data leakage. Our study focuses on the FirmCore cohesive subgraph model, which is challenging to compute using SMPC because it requires intensive interactions among providers. We propose a basic algorithm, SMPCORE, and two enhanced algorithms, SMPCORE-BP and SMPCOREAP, to exactly compute FirmCore subgraphs without revealing the providers' raw edge sets. SMPCORE-BP and SMPCOREAP balance efficiency and security by modifying SMPCORE's vertex-peeling strategy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMPCORE-BP and SMPCORE-AP improve performance by 1.7–7.7× and 2.4–8.2×, respectively, compared with SMPCore, while disclosing coarser-grained peeling traces.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3747794: Federated learning is highly vulnerable to poisoning attacks, where malicious participants attempt to corrupt the global model. Developing an effective defense remains challenging due to three coupled issues: the fundamental conflict between preserving strict user privacy and inspecting updates for malicious behavior, the massive computational overhead introduced by cryptographic protection mechanisms, and the non-independent and identically distributed ( non-IID) nature of user data, which heavily blurs the line between benign statistical variations and genuine malicious deviations. To address these issues, we propose a privacy-enhanced poisoning defense framework that selectively identifies and rectifies malicious parameter manipulations at a fine-grained level, rather than blindly discarding entire user updates. By isolating the critical parameter paths associated with poisoning behaviors, the proposed framework preserves useful benign contributions and mitigates main-task performance degradation, particularly under highly heterogeneous non-IID settings. In addition, the framework adopts a lightweight privacy-preserving architecture that protects raw user parameters while avoiding prohibitive cryptographic overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves strong poisoning defense capability and competitive main-task accuracy under adversarial non-IID environments. Cost analysis shows that the additional communication cost scales linearly with model size and the number of participating users, while the additional computation cost at each user scales linearly with model size.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3747924: This paper investigates communication-efficient layerwisefederated learning(FL) within resource-constrainededge intelligencenetworks. To facilitate effective layerwise FL in realworld scenarios, we consider the heterogeneities of CPU frequency, transmit power, time-varying channel states, and battery capacity of edge devices, and adopt a long-term perspective for the overall FL process. We formulate an optimization problem as amixed-integer nonlinear programmingproblem, aiming to minimize the overall learning latency associated with the layerwise FL process under per-device energy budget constraints. To solve this optimization problem, anonline optimization algorithm(OOA) based on Lyapunov theory is proposed, which realizes joint edge device selection and bandwidth allocation during the FL process. Furthermore, a detailed performance analysis of OOA is provided, demonstrating a trade-off between learning latency and energy deficit of the form [O(1/V) ,O(√V) ], whereVis a tunable hyper-parameter. Under the eight-device setting, simulation results demonstrate that applying OOA to layerwise FL reduces the overall learning latency and the overall energy deficit by an average of 7.14% and 67.73%, respectively, compared with layerwise FL under the original fixed uniform uploading schedule. Meanwhile, its overall learning latency remains only 2.03% higher than that of exhaustive search on average. The effectiveness of OOA is further verified when scaling up the number of edge devices and theconvolutional neural network(CNN) architecture.
10.1109/ton.2026.3747647: With the rapid advancement of edge computing, federated learning (FL) has become a widely adopted paradigm for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, especially when data privacy or limited computational resources prevent centralized training. However, even parameter-efficient methods like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) incur significant communication overhead in FL. Existing approaches to reduce this overhead, such as selectively freezing low-rank matrices, often compromise model expressiveness. To address these challenges, we propose CP-FedLoRA, a cross-layer co-designed framework spanning the model and physical layers for communication-efficient and privacy-preserving federated LoRA. CP-FedLoRA adaptively selects one of the two low-rank matrices for local training and integrates Count Sketch-based compression with AirComp aggregation to further reduce communication overhead and enhance privacy. We theoretically show that the sketching error, together with wireless channel noise, yields a closed-form privacy guarantee under zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP). We further establish a non-convex convergence bound for CP-FedLoRA and derive an optimal sketch-configuration strategy to balance privacy and model utility. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of CP-FedLoRA on both RoBERTa-base and Llama-3-8B. The results show that CP-FedLoRA consistently reduces communication overhead by 12.6%-19.9% on RoBERTa-base, while achieving comparable accuracy with over 20% reduction in communication overhead on Llama-3-8B, demonstrating its robustness across diverse model architectures and tasks.
10.1109/twc.2026.3747782: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) enables collaborative model training without central coordination. Gradient tracking (GT) improves the convergence of DFL under data heterogeneity but requires per-round connected topologies, inflating communication overhead. This paper proposes Dynamic AirComp-enabled DFL (DA-DFL), a framework integrating over-the-air computation (AirComp) on graphs with finite-time consensus. The key to DA-DFL is Periodically Anchored GT (PA-GT), which schedules additional local descent-tracking updates after the endpoint round of each consensus cycle. We derive a nonconvex convergence bound that decouples AirComp distortion from silence errors pertaining to sporadic withdrawal/absence of some users from model aggregations, revealing an irreducible error floor and yielding an approximate closed-form expression for the number of local steps. Based on the AirComp-dependent terms in the convergence bound, we minimize the per-round aggregation mean squared error via alternating optimization of the transmit and receive beamformers. Simulations demonstrate that PA-GT achieves a 25.3% relative accuracy improvement over baselines on graphs with finite-time consensus, and surpasses static connected topologies by 12.8%. DA-DFL limits accuracy degradation within 5% with beamforming at moderate SNR, and restricts performance loss to 1.4% when 20% of users are silent.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3747858: With the explosive growth of distributed data sources and increasing concerns over data privacy, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for privacy-preserving, distributed model training. However, traditional FL frameworks often underutilize the computational and data resources of the central server, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. Hybrid Federated Learning (HFL) addresses this issue by enabling collaborative training between the server and clients, but it introduces new challenges, particularly in handling server-client data heterogeneity—unbalanced, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) server data—a factor often underexplored in existing HFL studies. To tackle this, we propose FedATMV, a novel HFL framework that integrates Adaptive server-side Training (AT) and Model Variation (MV). FedATMV adaptively adjusts the server's training impact via a multifaceted scaling factor, considering server data proportion, non-IID degree, model accuracy, and recent performance trends, ensuring robust utilization of server resources and mitigating server-induced bias. Additionally, FedATMV generates diverse sub-models for clients by adaptively varying the global model, encouraging exploration of flatter regions in the loss landscape and enhancing generalization. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate FedATMV achieves relative accuracy improvements of 2.47%–31.20% over the best-performing HFL baseline across various heterogeneous settings, without incurring additional communication overhead.
10.1109/twc.2026.3747602: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices’ transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.
10.1109/tce.2026.3747682: Digital transformation in smart cities can enhance critical public services by using data from ubiquitous sensing and Internet of Things (IoT) sources. However, Emergency Medical Services routing often relies on static protocols or partial traffic data. This approach frequently ignores real-time hospital states such as equipment availability and Emergency Department crowding. Consequently, capability mismatches occur and lead to secondary transfers that compromise patient outcomes. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a “Digital Twin federation” architecture. This architecture integrates heterogeneous urban data streams into a unified decision-making framework. These streams include live traffic sensing, ambulance telemetry, and real-time hospital resource monitoring. The proposed system employs a rolling-horizon optimization controller. This controller uses the fused data to perform capability- and queue-aware routing without disrupting background traffic. We validated the framework on a calibrated scenario of Riyadh. The results show that exposing hospital-side IoT signals to the prehospital transport layer eliminates patient forwarding. It also significantly improves the Time to Definitive Care for critical cohorts like stroke and trauma. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven data fusion in establishing resilient smart city healthcare infrastructure.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3747377: Federated Learning (FL) is fundamentally challenged by statistical heterogeneity, where non-identically distributed (non-IID) data induces "client drift" that severely hampers global convergence. While existing approaches attempt to mitigate this drift through spatial-domain gradient correction or regularization, they overlook the intrinsic spectral structure of optimization signals. In this work, we revisit client drift from a frequency-domain perspective and empirically observe a "Spectral Bias of Drift": in the evaluated training trajectories, a disproportionate fraction of inter-client gradient disagreement is concentrated in the lower-frequency bands of the adopted structured parameter layout. Motivated by this observation, we propose SpecGradFilter, which suppresses a small low-frequency portion of selected layer gradients and can be implemented using an FFT-based projection or spatial-domain detrending approximations. For the FFT-based realization, we establish a conditional convergence guarantee when the projection retains sufficient global descent signal and the post-filtering client heterogeneity is bounded. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and additional benchmarks show improved accuracy and time-to-target in the tested non-IID settings without increasing the per-round communication payload.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3746978: This paper investigates a secure beamforming scheme for a cognitive satellite-terrestrial integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) network assisted by an active recon figurable intelligent surface (RIS). In this system, the active RIS is deployed to assist the terrestrial base station (BS) in suppressing cross-tier interference and enhancing the secrecy rate of primary users against potential eavesdroppers. We formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the radar output signal to-noise ratio by jointly designing the transmit beamforming at the satellite and BS, and the active RIS reflection coefficients, subject to constraints on secrecy rate, quality of service, and power budgets. To address the non-convexity and high complexity of this collaborative beamforming problem, we propose a federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (FMA-DRL) framework. Specifically, a federated deep deterministic policy gradient (F-DDPG) algorithm is developed, where the satellite and BS act as independent agents to cooperatively learn the optimal policy in a distributed manner. Moreover, this algorithm supports continuous action spaces, where agents only transmit action information and shared backbone parameters during cooperative training instead of raw local channel data. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed active RIS assisted scheme significantly outperforms the passive RIS benchmark in terms of both secure transmission and sensing capabilities within the cognitive satellite-terrestrial network.
10.1109/tfuzz.2026.3747269: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly been used for fuzzy systems given it allows interpretable and collaborative modeling across decentralized data environments. However, the inherently linear regression structure of Takagi–Sugeno (TS) fuzzy models makes their transmitted parameters or gradients in FL susceptible to inferring both antecedent and consequent components, thereby exposing sensitive information about the underlying client samples. Although defense strategies developed for general machine learning models exist, these methods often disrupt the fine-grained parameter structure that TS models rely on, leading to a substantial loss in predictive performance. For this reason, achieving a meaningful balance between privacy and utility when transmitting the parameters of TS models remains a central challenge in federated fuzzy learning. To address this issue, we developed a trilevel framework, to strengthen privacy when training TS fuzzy models in federated settings. The top level acts as an obfuscator, while the middle and bottom levels form a bilevel reconstruction attacker. In effect, this establishes an adversarial structure in which the obfuscator learns to counter a stable and realistic attack. By optimizing directly against the attacker's reconstruction risk, the framework learns perturbations that improve privacy without sacrificing the model's utility. Experiments conducted in both the standard multi-sample client setting and the challenging single-sample client setting show that the proposed framework yields substantially higher reconstruction errors for both the antecedent and consequent parameters. Additionally, the prediction performance is comparable to FedAvg, outperforming the representative federated defenses in terms of the overall balance between privacy and utility.
10.1109/tifs.2026.3746765: This paper studies differentially private (DP) graph synthesis in federated settings, where each client holds a local subgraph. While existing DP graph synthesis methods assume a centralized data model, their direct deployment in federated environments suffers from severely degraded utility. To bridge this gap, we introduce FGDPsyn, a novel framework for federated DP-compliant graph synthesis. FGDPsyn treats the nodes within a client as an atomic unit and aggregates global structural statistics in a client-wise fashion. A key challenge in this setting is the linear growth of accumulated DP noise with the number of participating clients. To mitigate its impact on synthesis quality, FGDPsyn incorporates an adaptive threshold-based clipping technique that removes unreliable intersubgraph edge statistics, thereby enhancing robustness to noise. We further propose a fine-grained link construction mechanism that progressively incorporates selected edges into inter-subgraph statistical estimation until a confidence threshold is met, naturally introducing heterogeneity in edge participation across the federation. To leverage this heterogeneity, we adopt a heterogeneous-aware information extraction mechanism that fully exploits the varied edge participation characteristics, thereby achieving nearcomplete utilization of the privacy budget. Experiments demonstrate that FGDPsyn generates synthetic graphs with high utility across multiple metrics.
10.1109/tim.2026.3747116: Acoustic diagnosis of wind turbine blades (WTBs) relies on measurements acquired by distributed sensing nodes under varying environmental and operating conditions. Such variations may contribute to differences in acoustic data distributions across wind farms. Centralized training requires transferring raw acoustic data from multiple wind farms to a central server, incurring communication overhead. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a distributed acoustic measurement and diagnosis system for WTBs. The proposed system integrates non-contact sensing, local signal processing, and federated learning while maintaining raw acoustic data locally. FedReP (Federated Representation and Personalization Learning) is the federated diagnosis module, where client-specific prompts provide local adaptation and prototype anchoring regularizes shared fault representation learning across wind farms. A stage-specific optimization strategy assigns different objectives to prompt adaptation and backbone refinement under heterogeneous sensing conditions. For edge-side deployment, a compact acoustic encoder, PRePNet, extracts non-stationary time-frequency features with low computational complexity. Experiments on field-collected multi-farm acoustic datasets and a public laboratory dataset show competitive diagnostic performance among representative federated baselines. On-device evaluation on NVIDIA Jetson TX2 NX further reports a local preprocessing to classification latency of 25.744 ± 1.726 ms per 2 s window under the tested configuration.
10.1109/tnsm.2026.3747185: The rapid scaling of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven the adoption of Multi-LoRA as a lightweight mechanism for model customization. However, deploying Multi-LoRA in edge federations introduces significant challenges in operational expenditure (OPEX) and latency efficiency. In this paper, we introduce a semantic-aware Multi-LoRA serving framework for edge federations that jointly optimizes OPEX and Quality of Experience (QoE). Specifically, we propose a semantic compatibility model based on behavioral embeddings to enable high-fidelity LoRA substitution, thereby reducing cold-start latency and redundant cross-region data transfers. We further develop a hierarchical multi-timescale architecture that separates long-term model provisioning from real-time request dispatching, allowing the system to adapt to dynamic workload skewness under data sovereignty constraints. Additionally, we design a Lyapunov-based dynamic dispatching algorithm to jointly optimize cross-cluster routing, node auto-scaling, and VRAM execution modes in real time. Extensive discrete-event simulations based on real-world Microsoft Azure Functions traces demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly mitigates the batch-squeezing effect and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in steady-state throughput, long-term OPEX reduction, and 95th-percentile Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) Service Level Objective (SLO) compliance.
10.1109/tii.2026.3726693: The large amount of heterogeneous data poses challenges to the imputation of data from the solid waste treatment. The popular imputation models like RNNs and Transformers ignore the heterogeneity among sensor data. To address the interaction effects among heterogeneous sensor data, a spatially aware lightweight GNN imputation method (SALG) is proposed. First, a lightweight temporal embedding method is designed to recognize complex multilevel dependencies using multilayer linear embedding modules. Second, a spatial conditional attention mechanism is developed to model nested-derived heterogeneous information by leveraging nested-derived edge vectors. The spatial conditional attention method captures heterogeneous spatio-temporal features. Third, a parallel spatio-temporal heterogeneity-aware prototype federated learning method is designed, employing spatio-temporal heterogeneity relationships as prototypes to parallel communications. The proposed SALG produces more accurate imputation results than the comparison methods on three benchmark datasets and two solid waste treatment datasets.
10.1109/tce.2026.3746576: The proliferation of portable uterine ultrasound devices promises enhanced accessibility for women’s healthcare, yet intensifies critical challenges in data privacy, resource limitations, and data silos for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostics in consumer electronics. Traditional centralized learning is infeasible due to highly sensitive patient data and constrained edge device capabilities. This paper proposes Sec-UterUS-CLIP, a novel privacy-preserving cloud-edge collaborative learning framework for uterine ultrasound diagnostics. Sec-UterUS-CLIP integrates a semantic similarity-enhanced vision-language model UterUS-CLIP as the local learning backbone, which is initialized via cloud pre-training and refined through federated fine-tuning across decentralized consumer devices by exchanging only model parameters. Crucially, we introduce a noise-resilient alignment strategy that leverages semantic similarity constraints to counteract the utility loss caused by differential privacy (DP) noise injection. This approach enables robust client model updates under different privacy perturbation levels, heterogeneous client distributions, and varying federated deployment scales. Evaluated on the large-scale UterUS-11K dataset, Sec-UterUS-CLIP achieves performance comparable to centralized models, while enhancing privacy through a client-level privacy-preserving Gaussian perturbation mechanism. This work establishes a practical paradigm for secure, intelligent, and scalable AI integration into resource-constrained consumer healthcare devices.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3746712: The low-altitude economy (LAE) is a rapidly emerging paradigm that builds a service-centric economic ecosystem through large-scale and sustainable uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled service provisioning, reflecting the transition of the 6G era from technological advancement toward commercial deployment. The significant market potential of LAE attracts an increasing number of service providers (SPs), resulting in intensified competition in service deployment. In this paper, we study a realistic LAE scenario in which multiple SPs dynamically deploy UAVs to deliver multiple services to user hotspots, aiming to jointly optimize communication and computation resource allocation. To resolve deployment competition among SPs, an authenticity-guaranteed auction mechanism is designed, and game-theoretic analysis is conducted to establish the solvability of the proposed resource allocation problem. Furthermore, a resilient federated reinforcement learning (FRL)-based solution is developed with strong fault tolerance, effectively countering transmission errors and malicious competition while facilitating potential cooperation among self-interested SPs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves service performance and robustness compared with baseline methods, providing a practical and scalable solution for competitive LAE service deployment.
10.1109/tcss.2026.3738284: Federated learning (FL) breaks down data silos through distributed collaboration. Due to the limited motivation of participants, incentive mechanisms are essential for encouraging sustained participation. However, existing incentive mechanisms are vulnerable to free-rider attacks, particularly in differentially private FL (DPFL), where the injected privacy noise obscures intrinsic gradient characteristics and significantly degrades the effectiveness of existing free-rider detection methods. Moreover, most existing incentive mechanisms adopt conventional aggregation strategies without incorporating participant contributions, thereby limiting the performance of the global model. To address these challenges, this article proposes an efficient incentive mechanism against free-rider attacks for DPFL, called incentive mechanism against free-rider (IMFR). Specifically, the central server detects free-riders by performing linear regression on the cosine similarities of consecutive local updates and records their historical behaviors. Based on the historical free-riding behavior, local data size, and privacy budget of each participant, IMFR evaluates participant contributions and performs contribution-weighted model aggregation to improve the quality of the global model. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that IMFR satisfies long-term incentive compatibility, individual rationality, budget feasibility, computational efficiency, low storage overhead, differential privacy guarantee, and aggregation stability. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that IMFR consistently achieves superior free-rider detection accuracy, incentive effectiveness, and aggregation performance compared with existing methods.
10.1109/tsc.2026.3744791: Dynamic fog-cloud task offloading requires coordinated decisions under time-varying workload, resource, energy, and network conditions. Existing approaches do not adequately couple future workload/Quality of Service (QoS) prediction with constraint-feasible allocation, adaptive policy refinement, and collaborative workload redistribution. To address this gap, this paper proposes Structured Predictive Energy-Constrained Convex Optimization (SPEC-CO)-Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), which integrates predictive workload/QoS estimation, prediction-conditioned convex allocation, DRL-based policy refinement, and collaborative fog-node federation. The framework is evaluated using the Intel Berkeley, Edge-Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Solar datasets in a simulated fog-cloud environment comprising 20 fog nodes, 2 cloud servers, and 100 IoT devices over 1000 Monte Carlo runs. Across the evaluated scenarios, SPEC-CO-DRL achieves 12.8-25.1 ms latency, 93.4-98.5% task completion, 27.8-42.3 J/task energy consumption, 75.2-85.7% renewable-energy utilization, and 85.4-92.5% federation efficiency. Relative to the evaluated baselines, it reduces latency by up to 35.4%, energy consumption by 33.8%, and the reported privacy metric by 74.4%. These results demonstrate that explicit coupling of prediction, feasible optimization, adaptive refinement, and collaborative redistribution improves QoS-aware offloading under dynamic fog-cloud conditions.
10.1109/tce.2026.3745550: Multi-omic cancer subtyping clusters tumors according to their molecular characteristics and clinical manifestations, serving as the basis for personalized diagnosis and treatment. However, existing federated subtyping models face two critical challenges: (1) they neglect intrinsic relationships among low-dimensional features, and (2) they construct sample similarities directly from these unpurified features, yielding unreliable representations. To tackle these problems, a model named Federated Multi-omic Cancer Subtyping with Low-dimensional Feature Perception (FMCSLFP) is proposed. Specifically, high-dimensional multi-omic data is projected into a low-dimensional space for feature-wise self-representation learning. Furthermore, the ℓ2,1-norm and an orthogonality constraint are applied to the feature self-representation matrices to uncover relationships among low-dimensional features and enhance their representational capacity. Subsequently, the enhanced low-dimensional representations are utilized for sample-wise self-representation learning to generate similarity matrices, which are then stacked into a third-order tensor to explore high-order and low-rank information within the multi-omic data. An optimization algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is designed to solve the proposed FMCSLFP, effectively preserving data privacy by exchanging only model updates rather than raw multi-omic data across distributed devices. Extensive experiments are conducted on six cancer datasets, validating the model’s effectiveness for cancer subtyping.
10.1109/tmc.2026.3746625: The large-scale deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites enables distributed AI tasks within satellite-terrestrial integrated networks (STIN), while federated learning (FL) has addressed the challenges of data privacy protection and communication latency of the distributed AI tasks in terrestrial networks. However, the integration of LEO satellites introduces three fundamental challenges: intermittent ground-satellite connectivity, dynamic inter-satellite topology, and limited satellites computing resources. This work introduces a LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)-based federated fine-tuning (FFT) tailored for STIN to reduce computational and communication overhead.
